nodes.label: Hermes config deep-merge semantics
nodes.rationale: hermes_cli/config.py::_load_config_impl deep-copies DEFAULT_CONFIG and _deep_merges the user file over it on every read, with no reference to the schema version. Dict sections merge key-by-key but a list REPLACES the default outright — which is exactly the behaviour the narrowed platform_toolsets.cli list depends on, and why a partial config is safe.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Hermes
nodes.rationale: admins-only, deliberately narrower than 'anyone who can reach the hostname', because this agent holds a shell inside the home network. The redirect URI is not free-form: plugins/dashboard_auth/self_hosted::_validate_redirect_uri requires the path end in exactly /auth/callback before it will even bounce to the IDP.

nodes.label: Dashboard auth gate fails closed on non-loopback bind
nodes.norm_label: dashboard auth gate fails closed on non-loopback bind
nodes.rationale: Binding 0.0.0.0 arms upstream's auth gate, which refuses to start unless a DashboardAuthProvider is registered — the estate relies on this: HERMES_DASHBOARD_OIDC_* registers the bundled self-hosted provider against authentik. Verified: with the vars unset the dashboard logs 'Refusing to bind dashboard to 0.0.0.0'; with them set, / returns 302 to /auth/login?provider=self-hosted and /api/config returns 401. HERMES_DASHBOARD_INSECURE is a deprecated upstream no-op and must never be reintroduced — an unauthenticated public dashboard was the entry point for the MCP-config persistence campaign that drove agents into planting SSH backdoors.

nodes.label: Healthcheck on dashboard /api/health, not gateway /health
nodes.rationale: The dashboard's /api/health is an unauthenticated liveness probe by design (hermes_cli/web_server.py, no _require_token) returning {ok, version, auth_required}. The gateway's /health on 8642 only exists when the OpenAI-compatible API server runs, and that server is deliberately off — so this is the stack's only HTTP health surface, a second reason the dashboard ships. start_period 180s because first boot seeds the data volume and starts the supervision tree, comfortably slower than the 30s interval on a cold LXC.

nodes.label: In-container dashboard (HERMES_DASHBOARD=1)
nodes.rationale: Running the dashboard as an s6-supervised service inside the same container is why upstream's `network_mode: host` is unnecessary: upstream ships the dashboard as a second container needing a shared PID namespace with the gateway for liveness detection, which forces host networking. In-container there is no namespace to share and the question disappears. Verified against v2026.7.30: single container, bridged, dashboard healthy.

nodes.label: _config_version: 33
nodes.rationale: Without the key the container logged '[config-migrate] WARNING: This config predates version 12 (~2 years old)' on every boot. Two upstream paths disagree: hermes_cli/config.py::migrate_config calls _raw_config_has_explicit_version() and treats a missing key as a fresh minimal config (so the CLI would migrate and stamp normally), but scripts/docker_config_migrate.py — what actually runs at boot — coerces a missing key to 0 via check_config_version(), takes the below-floor branch, prints the warning and returns 0 without ever calling migrate_config. Crucially the file was NOT discarded: the below-floor branch is warn-and-continue, config_migrations.py documents the file as left byte-for-byte untouched, load_config() has no version gate, and tools_config.py::_get_platform_tools reads platform_toolsets off the merged config — containment was in force the whole time. 33 is DEFAULT_CONFIG['_config_version'] in hermes_cli/config_defaults.py at the pinned tag, so docker_config_migrate.py short-circuits at current_ver >= latest_ver and never runs a migration pass that would strip every comment. When Renovate bumps the image and raises the latest version, the boot migrator rewrites the LIVE config (comments included) — normal, but bump this number when re-seeding a rebuilt host.

nodes.label: Narrowed platform_toolsets.cli
nodes.rationale: Kept: web, terminal, file, skills, todo, memory, session_search, clarify — enough to be useful while the shell stays the only high-power verb, contained by the container boundary. Removed with reasons: code_execution spawns a HOST subprocess from the agent's own interpreter, bypassing terminal-backend isolation, and terminal already covers running things with better guards; cronjob lets the agent schedule its own recurring work, a persistence mechanism matching the shape of the June 2026 MCP-config persistence campaign; delegation spawns sub-agents, multiplying spend and obscuring the audit trail; browser needs BROWSERBASE_API_KEY (external cloud browser with residential proxies and CAPTCHA solving) and is inert without it, listed so 'off' is a decision not an accident; computer_use has no display; vision/image_gen/tts/stt need provider keys not set. UNVERIFIED caveat: bfl reports enabled even when omitted, apparently registering outside platform_toolsets — inert without an API key but worth investigating if the toolset list ever seems not to apply.

nodes.label: Gatus assertion: auth_required == true
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing condition, not a nicety: it is the regression alarm for the dashboard's auth gate — if the OIDC env vars go missing or get misconfigured the gate disengages and this check fires, where a plain 200 would not catch it. A check asserting / 302s to the authentik login was DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED: unauthenticated / does return 302, but whether Gatus reports 302 or silently follows to authentik's 200 login page depends on redirect handling this repo has no prior art for, so the assertion would be a coin flip.

nodes.label: homelable-view-block Traefik router
nodes.rationale: LIVEVIEW_KEY enables a read-only canvas that bypasses OIDC entirely, and the key travels in a query string — traefik's accessLog (format: common, filters.statusCodes includes 200) writes the full request line, so every SUCCESSFUL live-view load logs the key in plaintext; it also lands in browser history and any outbound Referer. So /view is not served on the LAN-facing hostname at all and live view is tailnet-only, where every viewer is Tailscale-authenticated under the ACLs in git and a compromised device on the flat 10.10.0.0/16 cannot reach it. TWO paths must be blocked: /view (the SPA page, frontend/src/main.tsx switches on pathname === '/view') and /api/v1/liveview (the data endpoint, backend/app/api/routes/liveview.py, key-authenticated only and NOT session-guarded — blocking the page alone would leave the whole topology readable as JSON). /api/v1/liveview/config is deliberately not blocked: it is OIDC-session-guarded and is what the UI reads to build a share link. Priority is pinned to 1000 because default priority is rule length and the main router's rule is ~30 chars. This router is the entire control.

nodes.label: Gatus check: Live View Blocked
nodes.rationale: Asserts [STATUS] != 200 on https://homelable.<domain>/view. If the blocking router is removed, reordered, or out-prioritised, /view starts answering 200 on the LAN-facing hostname and this fires. Any other outcome (404 from error-pages, 502 if error-pages is down) still passes, so it only alerts on the thing that actually matters.

nodes.rationale: prometheus-community blackbox exporter, fullnameOverride blackbox-exporter, readOnlyRootFilesystem with NET_RAW added so the icmp prober can open raw sockets; ServiceMonitor enabled at 1m/10s so Prometheus scrapes probe results.

nodes.rationale: dependsOn prometheus/observability because the chart's ServiceMonitor needs the Prometheus operator CRDs present; wait: false so a slow probe rollout does not block dependents.

nodes.label: Blackbox probe module: dns_soa
nodes.rationale: Queries the SOA of dns.driscoll.tech, so the estate's split-horizon DNS servers are health-checked on authority rather than plain reachability.

nodes.label: Blackbox probe module: http_2xx
nodes.rationale: Default HTTP health probe: HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.0, follows redirects, forced to ip4 so dual-stack targets do not probe over IPv6.

nodes.label: Blackbox probe module: http_404
nodes.rationale: Inverse probe that treats HTTP 404 as the success condition, for endpoints whose liveness signal is a deliberate not-found.

nodes.label: Blackbox probe module: icmp
nodes.rationale: Ping prober; the reason the pod securityContext has to add the NET_RAW capability.

nodes.label: Blackbox probe module: ssh_banner
nodes.rationale: TCP prober with a query_response expecting ^SSH-2.0-, so a listening-but-broken sshd fails the probe.

nodes.label: Blackbox probe module: tcp_connect
nodes.rationale: Bare TCP reachability probe for services with no HTTP surface.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition CRD (driscoll.dev/v1)
nodes.rationale: Namespaced CRD, auto-generated from a Rust ApplicationDefinitionSpec via the `CustomResource` derive. It is the estate's per-app declaration surface: identity (name/category/slug/icon/url), access policy, uptime monitoring, Gatus endpoints and Authentik provider config, all read downstream by the Pulumi applications stack.

nodes.label: ClusterDefinition CRD (driscoll.dev/v1)
nodes.rationale: Cluster-scoped sibling of ApplicationDefinition, also derived from a Rust ClusterDefinitionSpec. Carries per-cluster branding and the required name+domain that app URLs are composed against.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: application-definition-crds
nodes.rationale: deletionPolicy: Orphan so a churned or renamed Kustomization cannot garbage-collect the CRDs (and with them every ApplicationDefinition in the estate). See docs/cluster-consolidation/27-migration-churn-failure-modes.md.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition spec.authentik (SSF/SCIM/SAML provider config)
nodes.rationale: Per-app Authentik provider surface: ssf (shared signals), scim (token+url required), saml, and Google Workspace provisioning. Consumed by the authentik Pulumi stack.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition spec.authentikFrom (configMap/secret indirection)
nodes.rationale: Same configMap/secret indirection shape as spec.uptimeFrom, applied to the Authentik block which carries SCIM tokens and signing keys.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition spec.gatus (Gatus endpoints)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors Gatus v5.36.0 endpoints[] and is kept in step with schemas/gatus.schema.json. The CRD carries NO x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields, so any key missing from this schema is silently pruned by the API server and never reaches the Pulumi stack that renders the Gatus config; `mise run codegen` fails the build when the CRD key set and the JSON Schema diverge. Endpoint-level disable-monitoring-lock is accepted but a documented no-op (Gatus reads it only from the top level of config.go) and is kept only because stacks/applications/kubernetes.ts still emits it.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition spec.uptime (Uptime Kuma monitor)
nodes.rationale: Full Uptime-Kuma-shaped monitor definition (http/method/accepted_statuscodes, retries, TLS material, basic/oauth/ntlm auth), the older of the two uptime paths carried alongside spec.gatus.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition spec.uptimeFrom (configMap/secret indirection)
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch letting the uptime block be sourced from a ConfigMap or Secret instead of inlined, so credentials never land in the CR body.

nodes.label: system/backups backend prefix mismatch
nodes.rationale: The system Stack CR points the operator at s3://home-operations/backups while stacks/system/.mise.toml points local runs at s3://home-operations/system — every other stack agrees with itself. In-cluster and local runs therefore write two different state locations, and migrating the wrong one silently loses the clusters/* outputs every other stack reads.

nodes.label: skystar as proposed test target (recommended, not decided)
nodes.norm_label: skystar as proposed test target (recommended, not decided)
nodes.rationale: A Dockge cluster on its own Proxmox host, so testing there cannot touch equestria or SGC by accident — and it is none of the three hosts this plan is rewiring. Caveat the discovery undersells: skystar already runs backrest, backups/rclone-sftp and a PBS instance, so it is the offsite backup replication target, not an empty box. Its slowest-measured write latency is irrelevant to test-target fitness and must not be mistaken for disqualification.

nodes.label: 04 — Pulumi state backend: Minio-on-truenas → Postgres DIY on celestia
nodes.norm_label: 04 — pulumi state backend: minio-on-truenas → postgres diy on celestia
nodes.rationale: Ten Stack CRs move off the s3:// backend to postgres:// DIY; Minio is retained as a versioned stack-export archive rather than decommissioned, because the Postgres backend still carries the [PREVIEW] label and deserves a documented path back.

nodes.label: 05 — Import audit
nodes.rationale: Every permanent `import:` resource option must be proven safe or removed before the DNS-heavy phases lean on this code path. Most of the acute risk turns out to already be closed.

nodes.label: celestia over alpha-site for the state backend
nodes.norm_label: celestia over alpha-site for the state backend
nodes.rationale: 'You can put identity on the Pi, or state on the Pi, but not both.' Concentrating the artifact needed to rebuild everything onto the box used for risky experiments — and, after piece 07, also holding SSO — would repeat the spike-concentration mistake this piece exists to fix.

nodes.label: Spike single-machine fate-sharing (the actual argument for the move)
nodes.norm_label: spike single-machine fate-sharing (the actual argument for the move)
nodes.rationale: One TrueNAS VM hosts the Pulumi state bucket, the VolSync restic repo, the nfs-csi share, the Thanos bucket and the PBS datastore mount — and no backup plan references the Minio dataset. If spike is what is being rebuilt, the estate has neither the state nor a backup of it. Moving state into Postgres puts it inside the existing pg_dump → backrest → PBS chain automatically.

nodes.label: The aborted cutover and the gate it earned
nodes.norm_label: the aborted cutover and the gate it earned
nodes.rationale: Steps 2-3 hold; steps 4-5 did not, because the estate's Pulumi state backend was broken for hours (pulumi-nodejs 3.257.0 'Invalid checksum provided' against Minio) without anyone noticing. The DNS names had already been released from SGC and then re-claimed, leaving both sides claiming them. New precondition: confirm stacks/home can complete a run BEFORE releasing any name from SGC — the release half is cheap to do and slow to undo. Also: the restored database ages from the moment it lands, so any retry re-runs the dump.

nodes.label: Nothing else new lands on this Pi
nodes.norm_label: nothing else new lands on this pi
nodes.rationale: alpha-site already hosts bao-transit (the sole unseal path for equestria's OpenBao) and bao-standby (the DR receiver) — neither existed when the July concentration-risk analysis was written. With authentik added, re-measured headroom is ~1.2-1.7 GiB, so the rule is load-bearing rather than advisory.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition CRD (driscoll.dev/v1)
nodes.rationale: Repo-local schema (schemas/definition.schema.json) describing each Dockge stack to the estate tooling: display name, category, icon, access_policy groups, optional authentik oauth2 client, and gatus endpoint definitions. It is the single declaration that drives SSO client creation and uptime checks for a docker stack.

nodes.rationale: Infrastructure category, access_policy groups friends+family, self-monitoring gatus check on its own URL.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Z-Wave

nodes.label: scrape_config_files glob loading
nodes.rationale: Host-specific scrape jobs are loaded via the scrape_config_files glob in docker/_common/prometheus/config/prometheus.yml. A file merely copied into the container is silently ignored unless the glob picks it up — the failure mode is a config that looks correct and does nothing.

nodes.label: Break-glass SOPS artifact set in bootstrap/openbao
nodes.norm_label: break-glass sops artifact set in bootstrap/openbao
nodes.rationale: Seven files (static-unseal, transit-token, pulumi-approle, pulumi-passphrase, recovery-keys, break-glass-approle, restore-test-approle) each unlock exactly one link of the chain; all are decryptable only by the estate age.key, and each must be sops --decrypt tested from a machine that is not alpha-site.

nodes.label: Two independent OpenBao auth paths inside one pulumi preview
nodes.norm_label: two independent openbao auth paths inside one pulumi preview
nodes.rationale: BaoClient does its own lazy AppRole login off BAO_ADDR/ROLE_ID/SECRET_ID inside the program; vals runs BEFORE Pulumi to resolve ref+openbao:// literals in mise's [env] and cannot do an AppRole exchange, so it needs a pre-minted VAULT_TOKEN. pulumi-env.sh feeds both from one SOPS-encrypted AppRole.

nodes.label: In-cluster sops-age Secret rotation
nodes.rationale: kustomize-controller decrypts with a mounted identity from kubernetes/flux/meta/sops-age.sops.yaml applied via scripts/bootstrap-apps.sh; after the sweep it must be re-applied on both clusters and trimmed to the surviving identity, otherwise Flux keeps a retired key alive.

nodes.label: 06 — One age key
nodes.rationale: Every .sops.yaml across four repos drops from three age recipients to one (equestria's). Decision D5, settled twice on the issue and not relitigable.

nodes.label: PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE moved into OpenBao (one chain, not two)
nodes.norm_label: pulumi_config_passphrase moved into openbao (one chain, not two)
nodes.rationale: Before 2026-08-12 the state passphrase was a SOPS-only secret independent of OpenBao; now it is age key → sops → AppRole → OpenBao like everything else, with a break-glass SOPS copy kept for when OpenBao is unreachable. Simpler to reason about, but no secret is exempt from 'OpenBao must be reachable' any more — including the one that decrypts Pulumi's own state.

nodes.label: mise [env] re-application clobbers hand-exported variables
nodes.rationale: ref+openbao:// values are deliberately left unresolved in the environment (mise re-evaluates [env] per shell load with no caching), so the real entrypoint is the .config/mise/tasks/vals-run task. Exporting a variable by hand and then calling mise run does not protect it — the .mise.toml value can win — so a smoke test must run from outside the repo tree or edit the .mise.toml itself.

nodes.label: All four repos must move together (divergence is a bug)
nodes.norm_label: all four repos must move together (divergence is a bug)
nodes.rationale: equestria-cluster, stargate-command-cluster, vault and home-operations all carry byte-identical recipient lists, and each file's own comment says so. Consolidating two repos and leaving two behind recreates the exact divergence all four files warn against.

nodes.label: Two never-re-keyed SOPS files (the undecryptable-window trap)
nodes.norm_label: two never-re-keyed sops files (the undecryptable-window trap)
nodes.rationale: .sops.yaml records POLICY, not whether each file was actually re-encrypted after the policy changed. Two SGC files (talsecret.sops.yaml, flux-instance/secret.sops.yaml) were never updatekeys'd and do not carry equestria's recipient — narrowing to one recipient first would make them permanently undecryptable. Run sops updatekeys on them while SGC's private key can still decrypt them, then audit every sops footer for the surviving recipient before touching any .sops.yaml.
nodes.source_location: The trap this plan almost inherited

nodes.label: Minio retained as a versioned stack-export archive
nodes.norm_label: minio retained as a versioned stack-export archive
nodes.rationale: A nightly CronJob shaped like history-pruner exports every stack to s3://home-operations/archive/<project>/<stack>/<timestamp>.json. B2 replication was recommended by discovery but the repo has no B2 integration despite CLAUDE.md listing an sdks/b2 directory (aspirational, not built) — so the archive rides celestia's existing backrest→PBS chain instead.

nodes.label: The live literal import on the home-operations Minio bucket
nodes.norm_label: the live literal import on the home-operations minio bucket
nodes.rationale: import: "home-operations" is a literal evaluated on every run, but the resource has no deleteBeforeReplace and does have protect: true, which refuses any delete without a manual unprotect — so the worst case is a loud protect error, not a silent live delete. Whether it re-imports every run is still unverified; the test is two consecutive previews with nothing else changing, because a single clean preview does not prove safety.

nodes.label: StandardDns imports are structurally inert (but the wire is still there)
nodes.norm_label: standarddns imports are structurally inert (but the wire is still there)
nodes.rationale: unifiId and cloudflareId are hardcoded undefined inside the only public entry point (StandardDns.create), whose signature exposes no id parameter — so no caller can arm the bug today. Residual risk: the private constructor still threads those params into import: + deleteBeforeReplace, so a future edit could re-arm it. Recommended cleanup is deleting the dead parameters entirely.

nodes.label: Minio bucket protect + retainOnDelete
nodes.rationale: protect: true refuses any delete without a manual unprotect, and retainOnDelete keeps data through a stack destroy — the guardrails the Pulumi state bucket relies on.

nodes.label: import + deleteBeforeReplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.norm_label: import + deletebeforereplace with a mismatched id format
nodes.rationale: When the supplied import id can never equal what the provider stores back in state, every run re-plans the same replace; with deleteBeforeReplace the destroy runs first. Cloudflare (<zoneId>/<recordId> vs bare recordId) wiped all 56 managed DNS records twice; UniFi (<site>:<recordId> vs bare) destroyed nine. Both fixes reuse the Pulumi resource NAME so a collision becomes a same-name replacement rather than an import.

nodes.label: Keep the archive bucket Pulumi-managed
nodes.rationale: protect + retainOnDelete only stay enforced and drift-checked while Pulumi manages the resource; unmanaging it moves the 'does this exist correctly' question outside the audit trail; and bucket versioning (minio.S3BucketVersioning) is only expressible as config if the resource stays managed.

nodes.label: Adopting existing mounts/auth backends requires pulumi import, one at a time
nodes.norm_label: adopting existing mounts/auth backends requires pulumi import, one at a time
nodes.rationale: Mounts and auth backends already exist, and a plain `pulumi up` fails loudly on a path already in use. Do NOT use the `import` resource option as a shortcut — the StandardDns/Cloudflare incident showed an id-format mismatch re-imports every run and, with deleteBeforeReplace, destroys live records.

nodes.label: Policies are the safe adoption starting point
nodes.norm_label: policies are the safe adoption starting point
nodes.rationale: vault.Policy create is a PUT, so adopting one is idempotent even without an import; the only consequence of Pulumi believing it created the policy is that destroy would remove it. Mounts and auth backends have no such forgiveness.

nodes.label: GrafanaDashboard: Flux Logs
nodes.rationale: Loki-backed log view; the reason flux.yaml declares a DS_LOKI datasource input alongside DS_PROMETHEUS.

nodes.label: GrafanaDashboard: AMD GPU (amdgpu)
nodes.rationale: Second vendor path: node_exporter --collector.drm (node_drm_gpu_busy_percent, node_drm_memory_vram/gtt_*) plus the amdgpu hwmon sensors (node_hwmon_temp_celsius, node_hwmon_power_*, node_hwmon_freq_freq_mhz). Two vendors with two data paths is why gpu.yaml ships two dashboards instead of one.

nodes.label: GrafanaDashboard: Intel GPU (Quick Sync)
nodes.rationale: Adapted from clambin/intel-gpu-exporter v0.7.1 (gpumon_* i915 PMU metrics), datasource swapped to $${DS_PROMETHEUS}, a `cluster` variable added so equestria and sgc render together through Thanos, and aggregations changed to keep `node` so multi-node selection stops averaging five GPUs into one line. grafana.com #23251 was deliberately NOT used: it targets the archived onedr0p/intel-gpu-exporter whose metric names do not match. Vendored (not grafanaCom id / url) to keep metric names pinned to the deployed exporter version.

nodes.label: $${DS_PROMETHEUS} double-dollar escaping for inlined dashboard JSON
nodes.norm_label: $${ds_prometheus} double-dollar escaping for inlined dashboard json
nodes.rationale: Inlined dashboard JSON is visible to Flux post-build substitution, which runs in strict mode and aborts the whole observability/grafana Kustomization on any ${...} it cannot resolve. Datasource placeholders are therefore written $${DS_PROMETHEUS}; the doubled $$ collapses to a single $ during substitution so grafana-operator still receives the token it maps via the datasources: inputName. Grafana's own template variables ($cluster, $node, $device, $__all) use the bare-$ form, which Flux does not touch, and are deliberately left unescaped.

nodes.label: GrafanaDashboard: Pecron Batteries
nodes.rationale: Battery/UPS view fed by the exporter in docker/alpha-site/pecron-monitor/, scraped by the alpha-site Prometheus and remote-written into Thanos; Grafana's default datasource IS Thanos Query so nothing extra is needed. Filter with {cluster="alpha-site", job="pecron"}. Deliberately NOT the hardcoded "uid": "prometheus" form used by cadvisor.yaml -- the Prometheus GrafanaDatasource sets no explicit uid, so the operator generates one and a hardcoded "prometheus" resolves to nothing. resyncPeriod 10m.

nodes.label: Hermes model provider (custom, llama-agent)
nodes.rationale: Hermes refuses to start its services with no provider configured — the boot log prints 'It looks like Hermes isn't configured yet' and s6 tears the container down (372 restarts before this was wired, 2026-08-03). base_url http://dockge-celestia.driscoll.tech:8081/v1 points at the llama-agent stack on the same host; the hostname resolves through Technitium split-horizon to the LXC's LAN address and llama-agent publishes 8081, so cross-stack container DNS is not needed and the traffic never leaves the LXC.

nodes.label: homelable-mcp container
nodes.rationale: tailscale entrypoint ONLY, deliberately no websecure router: MCP clients authenticate with a static X-API-Key header and cannot complete an interactive OIDC redirect, so authentik forward-auth would break this service rather than protect it. The boundary therefore has to be network-level — an endpoint whose only credential is a static key must not be reachable from the flat /16 this stack is about to scan. MCP_SERVICE_KEY (mcp -> backend) also bypasses OIDC by design, but only over the stack-private network, and the backend has no router at all.

nodes.label: llama-agent (llama.cpp Vulkan server) container
nodes.rationale: Hosts gemma-4-E4B on the Ryzen 5825U iGPU (RADV RENOIR) via /dev/dri plus group_add 992 (host render group). Decode ~10 tok/s and memory-bandwidth bound; prefill holds 100-125 tok/s out to 12K-token prompts. Published on 8081 because 8080 is taken by the _common llama-vulkan stack when deployed.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: llama.cpp Agent Server
nodes.rationale: Category AI, no access_policy or authentik block. Probed through Traefik rather than ${ipAddress}:8081 so the check covers the route Hermes' operators actually click; because the container port stays published, a failure here means 'hostname is broken' not 'llama.cpp is down'. /health only returns 200 once the model is fully loaded.

nodes.label: command: sleep infinity
nodes.rationale: With no CMD the entrypoint wrapper runs the interactive chat CLI, which exits instantly in a TTY-less container ('Input is not a terminal') and takes the container with it — the tail end of the restart loop. The main-hermes s6 service is deliberately a no-op and upstream's run script names `sleep infinity` as a preserved CMD contract for this dashboard-only deployment; sessions are driven by the dashboard over the `cli` platform.

nodes.label: -c 65536 -np 1 context/slot sizing
nodes.rationale: -np 2 splits the window into two 32K slots, and the PER-SLOT number is what llama.cpp advertises on /props and /v1/models — so Hermes read 32,768 and refused to boot against its own 64,000-token floor ('agent init failed: ...below the minimum 64,000 required by Hermes Agent', 2026-08-03). Hermes is the primary consumer so the window wins over slot count. Do NOT work around it with model.context_length in Hermes' config.yaml: that override exists for servers under-reporting a true window, and here 32,768 was the honest per-slot budget — the override would just move the failure to a mid-session context overflow. Losing the second slot costs little because decode is bandwidth bound (two slots split ~10 tok/s rather than adding throughput; concurrency only bought head-of-line avoidance). Keeping both via -c 131072 -np 2 is deliberately rejected: gemma-4-E4B has 4 unique global-attention layers at 2 KV heads x 512+512 f16 = ~16 KiB/token, so doubling the window adds ~1 GB and the host already sits on a full 1 GB swap with ~2.4 GB free. n_ctx_train is 131072, so 65536 is a serving choice not a model limit; KV + weights peak ~5 GB of the host's 7.7 GB GTT allowance, and GTT is HOST kernel memory not counted against the LXC cgroup.

nodes.label: No authentik middleware on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
nodes.norm_label: no authentik middleware on an openai-compatible endpoint
nodes.rationale: Same as docker/celestia/zot: these names resolve to the LXC's 100.x tailnet address in both split-horizon views (public Cloudflare included), so websecure here is tailnet/LAN-only, not an internet edge. A forward-auth gate would also break every OpenAI-compatible client on this hostname. The published 8081 stays, so the Traefik route is purely additive and nothing breaks if Traefik is down.

nodes.label: Host-level postgres database declarations (celestia)
nodes.rationale: Exists as the home for databases whose owning stack no longer exists — an x-postgres block needs a stack to live in, so an orphaned role/database (e.g. forgejo after its move to equestria) has nowhere else to be declared. Parsed by components/dockerStackPostgres.ts into the postgres stack's generated .env-local.

nodes.label: ExternalName + tailnet-inbound ProxyGroup route to celestia Postgres
nodes.norm_label: externalname + tailnet-inbound proxygroup route to celestia postgres
nodes.rationale: The shared _common postgres publishes no ports and is reachable only from dockge_default, so both workspace pods and laptops are outside it. The fix reuses the existing kubeproxies pattern: an ExternalName Service annotated tailscale.com/tailnet-fqdn + proxy-group: tailnet-inbound, plus a tcp:5432 ACL grant modelled on the existing baoDumps tcp:2023 grant.

nodes.label: PGAPP_<NAME>_PASSWORD provisioning convention
nodes.rationale: One line in docker/<host>/postgres/.env-local becomes a login role plus an owned database on the next idempotent postgres-provision run, because DockgeLxc merges docker/_common/<stack>/ with docker/<host>/<stack>/ per relative path (host files win). Adding a database therefore needs zero changes in stacks/backups — the per-host backrest plan already covers /opt/stacks-data and postgres-backup already dumps every database.

nodes.label: ensure: absent tombstone (retain-by-default drop protocol)
nodes.rationale: Removing an entry never drops anything — retain is the default. Dropping a database requires declaring `ensure: absent`, deploying, and only then deleting the entry, so an accidental deletion from the file can never destroy data.

nodes.label: USB-SATA fsync/FUA test on sda (hard prerequisite)
nodes.norm_label: usb-sata fsync/fua test on sda (hard prerequisite)
nodes.rationale: node_disk_write_time_seconds_total measures request service time, not REQ_OP_FLUSH. USB-SATA/NVMe bridges either serialize fsync slowly or silently ignore FUA — the second is data loss on a power cut, not a latency number. This is a correctness signal that must be tested before Postgres lands, not optional due diligence.

nodes.label: Reuse the shared _common Postgres instead of a dedicated container
nodes.norm_label: reuse the shared _common postgres instead of a dedicated container
nodes.rationale: The generic shared-Postgres pattern did not exist on alpha-site in July; now it does, so declaring PGAPP_AUTHENTIK_PASSWORD gets the pg_dump → backrest → PBS chain for free as existing generic infrastructure, costs one fewer Postgres process on thin headroom, and one fewer thing to fsync-test and monitor. The restore half of the chain still has to be proven separately.

nodes.label: baoKvSecret sets retainOnDelete — old paths need hand-deletion
nodes.norm_label: baokvsecret sets retainondelete — old paths need hand-deletion
nodes.rationale: Removing a Pulumi write does not delete the KV path, so a migration that only edits code leaves the old value live and readable until someone runs `bao kv metadata delete`.

nodes.label: vault#127 — etcd fsync starvation on fluttershy/kerfuffle PNY SATA disks
nodes.norm_label: vault#127 — etcd fsync starvation on fluttershy/kerfuffle pny sata disks
nodes.rationale: Those nodes install /var (and therefore etcd) on a 27ms-write-latency SATA SSD while the fast NVMe is fully allocated to Longhorn; a write-heavy pod (pulumi Workspace, ~71% of the disk load) pushes etcd past its 10ms p99 fsync budget and cascades into cluster-wide leader-election losses. The durable fix is piece 19 turning those nodes into workers, so the interim mitigation is only a nodeSelector pinning Workspace pods away.

nodes.label: volsync-mover-nfs MutatingAdmissionPolicy injects the per-cluster repository mount
nodes.norm_label: volsync-mover-nfs mutatingadmissionpolicy injects the per-cluster repository mount
nodes.rationale: RESTIC_REPOSITORY renders as the in-container path /repository/${APP}, which looks cluster-global; the actual filesystem location comes from an admission policy that mounts nfs path /mnt/stash/backup/${CLUSTER_CNAME}/volsync onto every volsync-* mover Job. CLUSTER_CNAME arrives via the cluster-secrets substitution patch injected by the root cluster-apps Kustomization.

nodes.label: 01 — Stabilise (consolidation Phase 0)
nodes.rationale: First gate on the critical path 01 → 10 → 18 → 19 → 20; nothing that touches a node starts until its exit gate is green. Standing rule: today's live reality wins over the July discovery text.

nodes.label: 02 — VolSync two-writer cleanup
nodes.rationale: The premise this piece was scoped around is wrong: there is no shared restic repository and never was, so the work drops from a data-safety emergency to ordinary decommissioning hygiene.

nodes.label: PITR is available-but-unrehearsed on both clusters
nodes.norm_label: pitr is available-but-unrehearsed on both clusters
nodes.rationale: The NoSuchBucket archiving failure was fixed and both clusters show 10 consecutive completed daily backups with a real recovery window, but nobody has restored into a scratch cluster and timed it — 'restores are rehearsed, not improvised'. So PITR is additive margin and does not replace the nightly logical dump each CNPG-touching step must still take.

nodes.label: Tracker state is stale in the better-than-expected direction
nodes.norm_label: tracker state is stale in the better-than-expected direction
nodes.rationale: Five of six open blocker issues were already resolved live while still marked open — so the exit gate must be re-verified against the clusters rather than trusted from the issue tracker or from a prior snapshot.

nodes.label: Vestigial static volsync PV as the source of the wrong premise
nodes.norm_label: vestigial static volsync pv as the source of the wrong premise
nodes.rationale: volume.yaml defines a Bound-but-unreferenced PV/PVC mounting the un-prefixed export; it is an abandoned early approach whose git history sits alongside the admission policy that superseded it. Reading the component file plus that PV, and missing the admission policy, produced the false 'one shared restic repo' conclusion.
nodes.source_location: Where the July research went wrong

nodes.label: RUNBOOK Scenario B — the break-glass standby is a procedure, not a command
nodes.norm_label: runbook scenario b — the break-glass standby is a procedure, not a command
nodes.rationale: bao-standby is deliberately stopped by default (compose --profile break-glass) so alpha-site does not permanently co-locate the transit-seal key with a live copy of everything it protects; the nightly dump also carries an age layer so possession of alpha-site alone is not enough. The monthly restore drill proves the dump restores into a scratch sidecar, not that a real pulumi preview can run against the standby — so the exit gate is a one-time rehearsal with BAO_ADDR pointed at the standby, then standing it back down.

nodes.label: shared/cloudflare-driscoll-tech is the estate's designated canary
nodes.norm_label: shared/cloudflare-driscoll-tech is the estate's designated canary
nodes.rationale: Three non-ESO consumers read it in lockstep: openbao-replica's CANARY_PATH health check (with the KV v2 data/ infix), bao-standby's restore.sh break-glass read, and components/globals.ts's Cloudflare provider. Recommendation: KEEP the path where it is.

nodes.label: The OpenBao catch-22 (GlobalResources cannot construct without a live OpenBao)
nodes.norm_label: the openbao catch-22 (globalresources cannot construct without a live openbao)
nodes.rationale: GlobalResources builds a BaoStore and makes seven getSecretByTitle calls before any stack code runs, on preview as well as up. OpenBao itself runs inside equestria (3-pod HA StatefulSet on the shared CNPG postgres) and is transit-sealed from alpha-site, so 'both clusters down' and 'OpenBao down' are nearly the same event.

nodes.label: Not to be confused with OpenBao's Postgres
nodes.norm_label: not to be confused with openbao's postgres
nodes.rationale: This piece's database is celestia's Docker-hosted Postgres reached over Tailscale; OpenBao's is the shared CNPG cluster inside equestria. Routing Pulumi state through the CNPG cluster would recreate the exact fate-sharing problem, just against equestria instead of spike.

nodes.label: concealed_fields custom metadata must carry over
nodes.norm_label: concealed_fields custom metadata must carry over
nodes.rationale: shapeItem throws on a path marked contains_secrets: true with no concealed_fields, and a path that silently loses the list downgrades every value to plaintext in Pulumi state — secrecy comes from custom_metadata, not from the value itself.

nodes.label: KV v2 has no rename — copy, repoint, verify, then metadata delete
nodes.norm_label: kv v2 has no rename — copy, repoint, verify, then metadata delete
nodes.rationale: Moving a path means write-new → repoint consumers → verify → delete-old. Always copy the value, never regenerate: a new crypto-key or secret-key makes stored data unreadable and a new session key logs everyone out.

nodes.label: resolveBaoPath: title-addressed reads do not follow the data
nodes.norm_label: resolvebaopath: title-addressed reads do not follow the data
nodes.rationale: components/store/bao.ts derives shared/<baoSlug(title)> from a 1Password-style title, so eight paths are addressed by title with no literal 'shared/...' string in the repo. Moving one of those requires editing the call site to getSecretByPath(...) — moving the data alone turns into a hard throw.

nodes.label: Eight ungated OnePasswordItem dual-writes
nodes.rationale: Nine call sites still write 1Password items on every apply; only the PBS one lacks an OpenBao mirror. Unlike OpenBao writes (gated by baoDualWriteEnabled) there is no 1Password dual-write gate — open question whether that redundancy is intentional.

nodes.label: ClusterDefinition
nodes.rationale: A single record (type, key, title, rootDomain, authentikDomain, secret, icon) drives DNS, Traefik, Authentik and UI branding per cluster, so adding a cluster is a data change rather than a code change.

nodes.label: ComponentResource pattern
nodes.rationale: Reusable infrastructure is expressed as classes with children parented to `this` and outputs registered via registerOutputs, so a child (e.g. DockgeLxc) can reach its parent's provider rather than constructing its own.

nodes.label: GlobalResources (central provider + credential wiring)
nodes.rationale: Every stack constructs GlobalResources first; it initializes all providers from credentials fetched at construction time, so a stack never has to know how a credential is obtained.

nodes.label: OPClient (1Password Connect client)
nodes.rationale: Fetches 1Password items by title; the guide presents it as the single read path for credentials, which the OpenBao migration later inverted (reads moved to BaoStore, OPClient became write-only).

nodes.label: Provider centralization rule
nodes.rationale: All providers are created in exactly one place (GlobalResources). Duplicating a provider inside a stack splits credential/state handling and is called out as 'NEVER DO THIS'.

nodes.norm_label: github_com_token from the reflected github app token
nodes.rationale: Renovate needs one — unauthenticated api.github.com is 60 requests an hour for the whole egress IP — but it already exists: the GitHub App installation token stacks/vault/KubernetesGithubAppToken.ts mints and emberstack reflects. It expires hourly and is re-minted, harmless because every Renovate pod is a short-lived Job. The driscoll.dev/token-expires-at annotation is the only non-secret evidence the value underneath is current.
nodes.source_location: There is no github.com credential to create

nodes.label: renovate-operator Policy Engine
nodes.rationale: Turned on though the chart ships it off. Bounds every URL taken from a RenovateJob: allowedHosts, allowedImages, and requireSecretRefOptIn (a Secret must label itself allow-ref: true). A policy denial leaves the job silently idle with Accepted: False — the condition's reason names the value to fix. Combined with rbac.ownNamespaceOnly so a RenovateJob elsewhere cannot borrow its credentials.
nodes.source_location: What the manifests already do — The policy engine

nodes.label: Renovate for Forgejo
nodes.rationale: Three pieces: the mogenius renovate-operator, one RenovateJob CR, and stacks/system/forgejo-renovate.ts which creates the bot account and mints its token. Split into two Kubernetes apps for the same reason garage-system splits cluster from operator — the second contains nothing but a custom resource whose CRD ships with the first's chart. Does not touch the GitHub side.

nodes.label: gitUrl endpoint — Clone Host Must Match Auth Host
nodes.norm_label: giturl endpoint — clone host must match auth host
nodes.rationale: Renovate keys its git credential to the host of `endpoint` (the in-cluster Service), but Forgejo advertises a public clone_url, so the two hosts differ and no credential matches. Discovery never notices because it only calls the API and never clones.
nodes.source_location: Troubleshooting — The executor fails on every repository

nodes.label: local> Presets Break on a Second Platform
nodes.norm_label: local> presets break on a second platform
nodes.rationale: local> resolves against whatever platform the bot is on, so on the Forgejo bot it looks for the repo on git.driscoll.tech instead of GitHub. .github/renovate.json5 therefore names its shared preset as github>david-driscoll/.github:renovate-config — identical on GitHub, and the only spelling that survives being consumed from a second platform. A new local> anywhere in the chain breaks Forgejo and nothing on GitHub.
nodes.source_location: Troubleshooting — Every repository errors with preset not found

nodes.label: Bridged Terraform Provider Version Lives in a base64 Blob
nodes.norm_label: bridged terraform provider version lives in a base64 blob
nodes.rationale: A Renovate bump is half a change and the missing half is silent: sdks/forgejo/package.json restates the version inside a base64 pulumi.parameterization.value, which is what the bridge actually resolves from. No regex can re-encode it, so a merged bump that was not regenerated reads 1.6.0 -> 1.7.0 while pulumi up keeps running 1.6.0 with no error. Also: `pulumi package add` rewrites its Pulumi.yaml entry as a BLOCK sequence while the Renovate customManager matches the flow form, so left as a block the provider silently stops being tracked.
nodes.source_location: Keeping the Terraform provider up to date

nodes.label: Forgejo ALLOWED_HOST_LIST for ClusterIP Webhook Delivery
nodes.norm_label: forgejo allowed_host_list for clusterip webhook delivery
nodes.rationale: Forgejo's default is `external` — valid non-private unicast IPs only — so without this every delivery to the operator's ClusterIP is dropped BEFORE it leaves the Forgejo pod, visible only in Forgejo's own delivery history. It names the exact host rather than the built-in `private` group on purpose: `private` would re-open delivery to every RFC1918 address, turning any repository's webhook settings into an SSRF primitive against the estate.

The profile mapping carries the groups claim the OpenBao roles bind on: admins -> admin policy, family -> viewer.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL storage backend (openbao_kv_store / openbao_ha_locks)
nodes.rationale: Storage is the shared CNPG cluster rather than integrated Raft, so leader election happens through openbao_ha_locks and there is no quorum to maintain. verify-full rather than require: postgres-rw...cluster.local is in the server certificate's serverAltDNSNames and ca.crt is the cluster CA. The URL carries no credential now that auth is the mounted client certificate, so it lives in git.

nodes.rationale: TLS terminates at the internal gateway and this listener is only reachable in-cluster, matching the other kube-system services.

nodes.label: Transit auto-unseal against bao-transit on alpha-site
nodes.norm_label: transit auto-unseal against bao-transit on alpha-site
nodes.rationale: The seal address must be the MagicDNS name reached through the tailscale-operator egress Service for dockge-as (pods have no tailnet route; both raw tailnet IPs were probed and unreachable). Leaving the address unset is NOT harmless: the wrapper falls back to api.DefaultConfig(), pointing the seal at this pod's own listener and deadlocking the unseal. VAULT_TRANSIT_SEAL_TOKEN is injected from the SOPS-backed openbao-seal Secret since nothing in-cluster can mint it.

nodes.norm_label: httproute bao.${cluster_domain} on the internal gateway

nodes.norm_label: nightly dump cronjob (pg_dump, age-encrypt, sftp to alpha-site)

nodes.label: Control-plane toleration via kustomize postRenderer
nodes.rationale: multus is a CNI DaemonSet: a node without it cannot attach secondary interfaces, so it must tolerate the control-plane taint that arrives with allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes: false. The patch REPLACES the whole tolerations list, so CriticalAddonsOnly is repeated to preserve it; re-diff against the chart's hardcodedValues when bumping the pinned digest.

nodes.label: Chart hardcodedValues wins the value merge
nodes.norm_label: chart hardcodedvalues wins the value merge
nodes.rationale: bjw-s common-library templates/common.yaml defines multus.hardcodedValues with controllers.multus.pod.tolerations, and that block wins against user values. Both controllers.multus.pod.tolerations and defaultPodOptions.tolerations were rendered locally with helm template and silently ignored, so the rendered manifest (postRenderer) is the only lever.

nodes.label: Gatus sys/health probe with standbyok
nodes.rationale: Probes the health endpoint rather than the redirecting UI root; standbyok=true so a standby answers 200 instead of 429, which would otherwise alert every time the route lands on a non-leader. A sealed node still returns 503 and an uninitialised one 501, so the page-worthy cases still fail.

nodes.label: ESO over reflector for CNPG-created Secrets
nodes.norm_label: eso over reflector for cnpg-created secrets
nodes.rationale: Both source Secrets are created by the CNPG operator, not Flux, so nothing in git can put reflector's reflection-allowed annotation on them — and reflector's explicit reflects: mode still requires it on the source. ClusterSecretStore/database is a kubernetes provider reading the database namespace directly. Everything lands in ONE Secret so there is one volume to mount and one object for reloader to watch, which matters because pgx reads the cert into tls.Config once at ParseConfig.

nodes.label: Superuser certificate kept in a separate Secret and mount
nodes.norm_label: superuser certificate kept in a separate secret and mount
nodes.rationale: openbao-pg-client-cert is the unprivileged storage identity; openbao-pg-admin-cert is a PostgreSQL superuser. Sharing a directory would put a superuser key one sslcert= typo away from the storage connection, and would make 'which cert does this path hold' a question rather than a fact.

nodes.label: Prohibition on disable_unauthed_generate_root_endpoints
nodes.rationale: Opened twice (#3067, #3078) because minting a root token from recovery shares had no other route; each time it meant two pod rolls and a public root-generation endpoint in between. Fixed by a break-glass AppRole whose only capability is opening an attempt on the authenticated endpoint (deny on secret reads and policy writes), with completion still requiring 3 of 5 recovery shares.

nodes.label: Certificate mounted as a volume so renewal rolls the pod
nodes.norm_label: certificate mounted as a volume so renewal rolls the pod
nodes.rationale: pgx reads the cert into its tls.Config once during ParseConfig at sql.Open, so a renewed certificate on disk is invisible to a running process. reloader.stakater.com/auto + RollingUpdate turns a renewal into a restart, and reloader only sees Secrets the pod actually mounts. defaultMode 0400 is hardening, not a requirement: pgx does os.ReadFile straight into tls.X509KeyPair with no permission check, unlike libpq.

nodes.label: RollingUpdate + reloader on the StatefulSet
nodes.rationale: Config is a ConfigMap read once at process start, so a config-only change leaves the pod template untouched and servers keep serving the OLD config while Flux reports success — that bit the OIDC bootstrap for 15h. Reloader rolls the StatefulSet on ConfigMap change, but is inert under the chart's default OnDelete strategy (the controller never replaces pods, and kubectl rollout restart refuses outright). OnDelete is right for Shamir-sealed upstream Vault; here transit auto-unseal makes rolling safe.

nodes.label: OpenBao is never a link in the chain that starts OpenBao
nodes.norm_label: openbao is never a link in the chain that starts openbao
nodes.rationale: external-secrets is a dependency only for ClusterSecretStore/database, a kubernetes provider reading the database namespace — not backed by 1Password today nor by OpenBao later. The seal token, which has no in-cluster source, comes from secret.sops.yaml. tailscale-services is a dependency because the unseal path runs through the dockge-as egress Service, without which pods crash-loop on a seal they cannot reach. Flipping suspend to false is a one-way go-live decision: the database will have been written to.

nodes.label: Two secret-bearing values, two deliberate sources
nodes.norm_label: two secret-bearing values, two deliberate sources
nodes.rationale: The Postgres connection URL comes from ExternalSecret via ClusterSecretStore/database so it rotates with the role without a second edit; the transit token comes from secret.sops.yaml because nothing in the cluster can regenerate it — it is minted against bao-transit and mirrored at bootstrap/openbao/transit-token.sops.yaml per bootstrap/INVENTORY.md. Everything else about the server config is plaintext in helmrelease.yaml.

nodes.label: Estate-wide shared rclone SFTP keypair
nodes.rationale: The same keypair DockgeLxc seeds onto every dockge host; its public half is already in authorized_keys on dockge-as, so shipping dumps needs no new key material anywhere. OpenSSH refuses a key file without a trailing newline, so the template appends one (DockgeLxc.ts:247 does the same).

nodes.label: Dump/restore trust boundary (no age identity on alpha-site)
nodes.norm_label: dump/restore trust boundary (no age identity on alpha-site)
nodes.rationale: Both cronjobs run in-cluster rather than on alpha-site so the dump can never be decryptable on alpha-site alone — that host also holds the transit key. The cluster already holds an age identity (Flux sops-age), so decrypting here adds no new exposure, and the restore test doubles as proof the dump left the building and can be fetched back. An unverified backup is not a backup (RUNBOOK Scenario D).

nodes.label: Gatus heartbeat via dockge-as egress with --connect-to
nodes.norm_label: gatus heartbeat via dockge-as egress with --connect-to
nodes.rationale: Pods have no route to the tailnet and no reachable DNS answer for uptime.${ROOT_DOMAIN}; Gatus is reported to through the dockge-as egress on 443, with --connect-to keeping Host/SNI intact so Traefik routes and the LE cert validates.

nodes.label: Literal PG_URI with client-certificate authentication
nodes.rationale: The dump used to authenticate with the openbao role's password over sslmode=disable; Phase 2.4b nulls that password and adds 'hostnossl openbao openbao all reject', either of which would break the job silently at 03:00. A certificate URI carries no secret so it needs no ExternalSecret — the credential is the mounted key. libpq enforces private-key permissions where pgx does not, so this was verified live (ssl=true, TLSv1.3, pg_dump exit=0) rather than assumed.

nodes.label: PGDATA subdirectory fix for Postgres 18 images
nodes.norm_label: pgdata subdirectory fix for postgres 18 images
nodes.rationale: Postgres 18 images refuse to start when the mount IS the data directory ('unused mount/volume'), and the pgdata emptyDir mounts exactly there. Pointing PGDATA at a subdirectory of the mount is the fix, matching docker/_common/postgres. Renovate crossed this major on its own once and broke the job silently for weeks (#835), which is why a renovate guard blocks majors for this image. Plain-SQL dumps restore into any equal-or-newer major, so the scratch engine only has to be >= the dump's origin major.

nodes.label: Deliberate omission of the postgres component
nodes.norm_label: deliberate omission of the postgres component
nodes.rationale: This app reads the existing openbao database with the credential provisioned for the openbao app; adding components/postgres would declare a SECOND database, role and credential named after this app. It dependsOn the openbao ks (not just postgres) so a half-initialised database is never dumped during bootstrap, and on tailscale-services because ports 2023/8200/443 to alpha-site exist only through the dockge-as egress Service.

nodes.label: Three-trust-root credential routing
nodes.rationale: ExternalSecret supplies the Postgres credential and the SFTP key (referenced, never copied); SOPS supplies the restore-test AppRole because it has no other in-cluster source; the transit seal token and the age identity are referenced from Secrets owned elsewhere (openbao-seal, sops-age) so a re-minted token never needs a second edit here.

nodes.label: Three estate age recipients
nodes.rationale: Must stay identical to .sops.yaml in this repo, vault, and stargate-command-cluster — a divergent set is how a dump becomes undecryptable by the one key that survives. No alpha-site-resident key is ever added: the host holding the ciphertext (and the transit key) must not be able to decrypt it alone.

nodes.label: Deliberate priority-value ordering for the low-power tier
nodes.norm_label: deliberate priority-value ordering for the low-power tier
nodes.rationale: Below system-cluster-critical (2000000000) and longhorn-critical (1000000000), above observability-critical (1000) and every unset pod. Priority governs preemption under contention, not placement: with workers powered off Tier-2 pods simply go Pending. The value of the class is the case where a control plane is LOST mid-window and the two survivors must evict the right things. Three same-named-looking objects, three kinds: this PriorityClass critical-tier, Longhorn's PriorityClass longhorn-critical, and piece 12's StorageClass longhorn-critical.

nodes.norm_label: longhorn ingress (internal class, traefik local-user middleware)

nodes.norm_label: storageclass parameters are immutable, so flux needs force

nodes.label: DEGOOG_DATA_DIR
nodes.rationale: Set explicitly rather than inherited from the working directory: plugins, engines, themes, server-settings.json and the indexer directory all derive from this one path (see paths.ts), so it is the single value that must agree with the volsync PVC mount point in helmrelease.yaml.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_VALKEY_URL (shared valkey db 9)
nodes.rationale: Points at the shared, password-less valkey in `database`. Database index 9 (8 is searxng, 6 is dispatcharr); degoog already namespaces keys by instance identifier, so the distinct index is tidiness that keeps a stray FLUSHDB from taking two apps down.

nodes.label: FlareSolverr Sidecar
nodes.rationale: A degoog transport backend running real Chrome to solve Cloudflare interstitials. Kept as a sidecar rather than its own app: degoog is the only consumer, and same-pod means the transport URL is http://127.0.0.1:8191/v1 with no Service, no route and no ingress. It gets plain env rather than envFrom degoog-env so a browser sandbox never holds the database password. The Store extension itself is NOT deployed by this file — installing it is a settings-page step.

nodes.label: Degoog search.* HTTPRoute (local-user)
nodes.rationale: Hostname is `search`, not `degoog`; TAILSCALE_HOST in ks.yaml carries the same name onto the tailnet. The route filters through the `local-user` Traefik middleware — a network gate with no authentik outpost.

nodes.label: Retrom Dropped Postgres Component
nodes.rationale: The components/postgres line is commented out rather than deleted because the whole ks.yaml is parked (group E drop, 2026-08-25). The Database CR, the database and the login role were all removed, so re-enabling the line does not restore the old state: the Pulumi `system` stack discovers the component and creates database/static-roles/${APP}, which fails outright until CNPG has recreated the login role.

nodes.label: Romm Gatus Low-Power Maintenance Window
nodes.rationale: Romm is scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly Low Power shed (docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md), so a failed Gatus check inside that window is expected rather than an incident. Gatus keeps checking and keeps the history; it just does not alert.

nodes.label: Romm Startup Probe Widening
nodes.rationale: The startup probe was widened from failureThreshold 3 (a 30s budget) to 300s ahead of putting romm's password on OpenBao rotation: a rotation is a forced restart and the pod's own conditions show Initialized->Ready taking 49s. tandoor (#1142) crash-looped six times on exactly this shape. Startup probes suppress liveness and readiness while pending, so this only widens the boot window; steady state is unchanged. Do not narrow it back.

nodes.label: Collabora SSL Termination Params
nodes.rationale: extra_params sets --o:ssl.termination=true --o:ssl.enable=false so Collabora Online serves plaintext inside the cluster and trusts the gateway to have terminated TLS; the container also runs with runAsNonRoot disabled because the CODE image expects to start privileged.

nodes.label: Degoog Authentik Forward Proxy
nodes.rationale: Forward proxy rather than oauth2 because degoog has no OIDC support at all; its only authentication is DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS, which gates the settings/extension panel and nothing else. The HTTPRoute still filters through `local-user`, a network gate WITHOUT the authentik outpost hop, because a search engine must answer OpenSearch and ?q= requests straight from the browser address bar and an outpost redirect breaks both. Same shape as searxng.

nodes.label: Degoog Gatus Low-Power Maintenance Window
nodes.rationale: Degoog is scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly Low Power shed, so failed checks in that window are expected and suppressed from alerting. The check targets /healthz rather than / so it does not run an actual search, and the route's own rate limiter applies to it.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_DISTRUST_PROXY Setting
nodes.rationale: Set to 0 (trust the proxy) — the variable is named for the negative, so the default of 1 makes degoog ignore X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP and every client looks like the Traefik pod, collapsing degoog's rate limiting and IP blocklist onto one source address. Safe only because the HTTPRoute through the internal gateway is the sole ingress path.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_POSTGRES Connection String
nodes.rationale: Built by hand instead of using the postgres_uri key, because that key carries ?sslmode=disable and degoog's driver (postgres.js 3.4.9) does `query.sslmode && (query.ssl = query.sslmode)` — the string "disable" is truthy, so the client opens TLS with rejectUnauthorized at its default, which fails against CNPG's self-signed CA and leaves the indexer silently at `adapter boot failed`. Omitting the query string keeps postgres.js at ssl: false, the plaintext connection every other app in the namespace makes to postgres-rw.

nodes.label: DEGOOG_SETTINGS_PASSWORDS
nodes.rationale: Read only from the environment — there is no settings UI or on-disk file for it. Left unset, degoog mints a throwaway password per process and prints it to the log, so on a restarting pod the admin panel password changes without warning; that panel installs extensions, and extensions run code on the server.

nodes.label: FlareSolverr /dev/shm tmpfs
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes gives 64Mi of /dev/shm and Chrome uses shared memory for renderer surfaces; past that it crashes mid-challenge and reads as a FlareSolverr timeout. Sized 512Mi rather than the usual 2Gi because `medium: Memory` counts against the container's own memory limit and a larger tmpfs could be filled to OOM the 1536Mi container. Mounted with advancedMounts so it applies only to flaresolverr.

nodes.label: Degoog Entrypoint Bypass (bun run)
nodes.rationale: The image ENTRYPOINT is bypassed with an explicit `bun run src/server/index.ts` command: entrypoint.sh does mkdir/chown on /app/data then su-exec, all of which need to start as uid 0 since the image sets no USER. fsGroup already makes the PVC group-writable by 1000, so the chown is redundant. Safe without a writable HOME because the image sets BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0.

nodes.label: Degoog /readyz Readiness Probe
nodes.rationale: Readiness targets /readyz rather than /healthz: degoog answers /healthz as soon as the HTTP server binds and only flips /readyz once markReady() runs at the end of boot, which is after the Postgres indexer adapter has connected.

nodes.label: Shared uid 1000 Pod SecurityContext
nodes.rationale: uid 1000 suits both containers by coincidence: degoog's base is oven/bun (user `bun`, uid 1000) and FlareSolverr's Dockerfile runs a bare useradd on python:3.11-slim, taking the first free id, also 1000. The numeric value is load-bearing because FlareSolverr's image declares USER by name, and with runAsNonRoot: true and no numeric override the kubelet refuses to start it.

nodes.label: New-App Postgres Ordering Trap (#1180)
nodes.rationale: Degoog is the app that found the new-app ordering trap: stacks/system raced Flux to the merge commit and died on `role "degoog" does not exist`. Read the ORDER OF OPERATIONS block in components/postgres/ks.yaml before adding components/postgres to a NEW app. The rotating credential is preflighted the way freshrss was — reloader.stakater.com/auto on the controller plus the credential arriving via the degoog-env Secret.

nodes.rationale: DNS traffic (53 UDP/TCP, 853 DoT, 443 DoH) lands directly on the dedicated interface, bypassing kube-proxy and any LoadBalancer service; the /16 broadcast domain means the same address is valid on either parent NIC.

nodes.label: emberstack reflector secret mirroring
nodes.rationale: The Secret carries no data of its own; it is filled by reflector from tailscale-system/tailscale-dns-authkey, whose source carries reflection-allowed=true.

nodes.label: Autobrr Authentik confidential OAuth2 client
nodes.rationale: Autobrr speaks OIDC natively, so it gets a real confidential OAuth2 client with two redirect URIs (public domain and tailnet domain) rather than the forward-auth proxy used by the Servarr-family apps in this directory.

nodes.label: postgres_ / oidc_ dataFrom rewrite pipeline
nodes.rationale: Two regexp steps normalise hyphenated credential keys into legal Go template identifiers and then namespace them. The credential Secret's key is `username`, so the template must say .postgres_username; .postgres_user renders empty and lib/pq silently falls back to the OS user (uid 568, no passwd entry), failing at connect time with a misleading error.

nodes.label: PROWLARR__LOG__DBENABLED toggle
nodes.rationale: Set to "True" now that the log database exists; it restores System > Logs in the UI and simultaneously makes the log database REQUIRED at startup. Flipping it back to "False" is the rollback if that database is ever missing.

nodes.label: bittorrent LoadBalancer service (TCP+UDP 18289)
nodes.rationale: A second Service on a pinned loadBalancerIP carries the torrenting port on both protocols, separate from the ClusterIP WebUI service that the Gateway routes to; UPnP is disabled because the address is assigned statically.

nodes.label: enp3s0 control-plane NIC as ipvlan master
nodes.norm_label: enp3s0 control-plane nic as ipvlan master
nodes.rationale: Changed from enp2s0 (worker NIC) on 2026-08-19 to move Technitium onto the control planes for low-power / battery mode; requires the technitium-dns=true node label set from talos/talconfig.yaml plus a matching pod nodeSelector.

nodes.label: ipvlan L2 instead of macvlan on Proxmox KVM nodes
nodes.norm_label: ipvlan l2 instead of macvlan on proxmox kvm nodes
nodes.rationale: macvlan would require promiscuous mode on the Proxmox vmbr bridge; ipvlan L2 shares the parent MAC so no Proxmox reconfiguration is needed.

nodes.label: Nightly Low Power Gatus maintenance window
nodes.norm_label: nightly low power gatus maintenance window
nodes.rationale: The service is scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly power shed, so a failed check in that window is expected. Gatus keeps checking and keeps the history but does not alert.

nodes.label: AUTOBRR__DATABASE_TYPE silent Postgres switch
nodes.rationale: internal/config/config.go gates the env value behind validDatabaseType, so a missing or invalid type is dropped silently and autobrr stays on SQLite with every POSTGRES_* var set and nothing logged. A bad databaseType in config.toml is ungated and hard-errors instead.

nodes.label: Default secretStoreRef corrected off onepassword-connect
nodes.rationale: Every dataFrom carries an explicit sourceRef so the default store was never consulted; it named onepassword-connect purely by template inheritance. Pointing it at the store actually in use removes a phantom 1Password dependency.

nodes.label: Startup probe buys migration time (autobrr)
nodes.rationale: First boot against an empty Postgres runs the whole migration chain and every 30-day password rotation forces a cold start. Without a startup probe the liveness budget is initialDelay + failureThreshold x period ~= 110s, so the kubelet kills the pod mid-migration and the restart replays it. A startup probe suspends liveness AND readiness, so 60 x 10s buys ten minutes and costs nothing on a normal boot.

nodes.label: Brand-new-app Postgres role race
nodes.rationale: autobrr had no database or role in the cluster when components/postgres was enabled (2026-08-26), so stacks/system creates the OpenBao static role before CNPG applies the DatabaseRole and stalls on 'role "autobrr" does not exist'. Expected; recovery documented in components/postgres/ks.yaml and the runbook.

nodes.label: Authentik forward_single proxy with /api bypass
nodes.rationale: Prowlarr has no OIDC support, so access is fronted by Authentik forward-auth. skipPathRegex '^/api([/?].*)?$' leaves the API key path unauthenticated so the *arr apps can keep talking to it machine-to-machine.

nodes.label: PROWLARR__SECTION__KEY prefix spelled out by hand
nodes.norm_label: prowlarr__section__key prefix spelled out by hand
nodes.rationale: The credential Secret's key names do not match the app's env var names and the upper-case prefix is not derivable from ${APP} (kustomize has no upper-case function), so each app spells its own five keys out instead of passing dataFrom straight through.

nodes.label: PROWLARR__POSTGRES__HOST as the Postgres on-switch
nodes.rationale: Sonarr-family apps use Postgres if and only if PostgresHost is non-empty (NzbDrone.Core/Datastore/ConnectionStringFactory.cs). Removing this ExternalSecret and its envFrom drops the app back onto the SQLite file still sitting in the config PVC - which is the rollback, and why that file is not deleted.

nodes.label: One credential, two databases (main + log)
nodes.rationale: ConnectionStringFactory builds both connections from the same PostgresUser/Password/Host/Port and varies only the database name, so there is no second role, no second OpenBao static role and no second password. LOGDB is a literal because the credential Secret describes only one database.

nodes.label: Startup probe buys migration time (prowlarr)
nodes.rationale: Same ~110s liveness budget problem as autobrr: an empty-Postgres first boot replays the entire migration chain and the 30-day rotation forces cold starts. 60 x 10s startup checks suspend liveness and readiness and cost nothing on a normal boot that answers /ping immediately.

nodes.label: POSTGRES_APP_PATH anchored to spec.path
nodes.rationale: components/postgres/databases appends /postgres-databases to POSTGRES_APP_PATH. Reusing the same YAML anchor as spec.path means the path is written once, so moving the app directory cannot leave a stale path behind.

nodes.label: postgres-databases deliberately excluded from the app build
nodes.norm_label: postgres-databases deliberately excluded from the app build
nodes.rationale: The directory sits inside the app's build path, so listing it in ../kustomization.yaml would render the Database a second time into the equestria namespace, where it is meaningless (CNPG resolves spec.cluster.name locally) and would fight the real one in the database namespace.

nodes.rationale: driscoll.dev/backup is an opt-OUT here (opt-IN for a Garage bucket) because the stakes differ. The database holds only app log entries that Prowlarr trims itself. backup-credentials is set as belt and braces: flipping the flag would otherwise send the backup looking for ${APP}-log-postgres, which does not exist, and one failed database exits the whole nightly job non-zero.
