nodes.rationale: Single rule through the network/internal Gateway with the Traefik authenticated-user middleware; unlike Lidarr there is no API-key bypass rule.

nodes.label: Kapowarr HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: app-template OCIRepository chart, Recreate strategy, digest-pinned mrcas/kapowarr, ClusterIP on 5656, config PVC mounted at /app/db.

nodes.label: Kapowarr TrueNAS Media Mounts
nodes.rationale: Shared truenas-media claim subPath-mounted as /downloads and /comics, the same claim every media app in this namespace attaches.

nodes.label: Kapowarr Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Depends on truenas-volumes, volsync and tailscale-operator; pulls in fast-node-eviction, tailscale and volsync components; substitutes APP/NAMESPACE.

nodes.label: Kometa ExternalSecret
nodes.rationale: Renders kometa-secret with seven KOMETA_*_APIKEY env vars from the openbao ClusterSecretStore: four cluster app credentials (plex, tautulli, radarr, sonarr) and three third-party vendor keys (tmdb, omdb, mdblist).

nodes.label: Kometa ConfigMap File Mounts
nodes.rationale: Each collection file is subPath-mounted read-only into /config, which is why the container can run with readOnlyRootFilesystem while Kometa still writes logs to the emptyDir.

nodes.label: ImageMaid CronJob
nodes.rationale: Runs 40 minutes after each Kometa pass in MODE: remove against the mounted Plex metadata directory, reclaiming orphaned Plex image bundles left behind by collection/overlay churn. Reads plex_token from spike-management-credentials rather than the kometa-secret.

nodes.label: Kometa CronJob
nodes.rationale: Eight-hourly CronJob running kometa.py twice (--run-libraries Movies then TV Shows) in read-only-config mode; hardened with readOnlyRootFilesystem, dropped caps and an emptyDir for /config/logs, and given 6Gi memory headroom.

nodes.label: Kometa Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Depends on plex (its target), external-secrets and volsync; unlike the Servarr apps it takes no tailscale or fast-node-eviction component since it is a batch workload.

nodes.label: kometa-configmap Generator
nodes.rationale: configMapGenerator with disableNameSuffixHash: true so the HelmRelease can reference a stable name kometa-configmap; the reloader.stakater.com/auto annotation on the CronJob is what turns a config edit into a new run.

nodes.label: Equestria Media App Index
nodes.rationale: Aggregates every media app's ks.yaml for the equestria cluster; emby, watchstate, tdarr and stremio are commented out rather than deleted, keeping them one line away from re-enablement.

nodes.label: Lidarr Postgres ExternalSecret
nodes.rationale: Renders the five LIDARR__POSTGRES__* env vars from the ${APP}-postgres credential in the database ClusterSecretStore. refreshInterval 4m matches the rotation ExternalSecret next to the credential so a rotated password reaches the pod before the old one is refused; deletionPolicy: Retain stops a provider blip from emptying the Secret the pod mounts.

nodes.label: Lidarr HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: app-template chart on port 8686 running as uid/gid 568 with supplementalGroups [44,109,10000]; auth method External with DisabledForLocalAddresses, so the Traefik middleware is the real gate. envFrom pulls the whole Postgres connection as one unit rather than five secretKeyRefs, and reloader.stakater.com/auto turns the 30-day rotation into a restart.

nodes.label: Lidarr TrueNAS Media Mounts
nodes.rationale: Same truenas-media claim as the other media apps, subPath-mounted as /media/downloads and /media/music — the shared download path is what lets the download client and Lidarr hardlink instead of copy.

nodes.label: Lidarr Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Adds components/postgres and components/postgres/databases on top of the standard media stack. POSTGRES_APP_PATH reuses the &path anchor so the databases component's appended /postgres-databases suffix cannot go stale when the directory moves.

nodes.label: Movie Chart Sort-Title Template
nodes.rationale: Chart/Chart Alpha templates encode display ordering into sort_title as ++++1.1_<<num>>, so collection ordering on the Plex home row is controlled by a numeric prefix rather than per-collection settings.

nodes.label: TV Chart Sort-Title Template
nodes.rationale: Uses the ++++2.1_ prefix namespace so TV collections sort after movie collections, and smart_label: random rather than an explicit collection_order.

nodes.label: Kometa Movies Library
nodes.rationale: Movies library loads the movie charts, best-of and holiday collection files; ratings come from IMDb genres plus MDBList tomatoes-audience/metacritic mass updates.

nodes.label: Kometa TV Shows Library
nodes.rationale: TV Shows library loads the TV charts and networks collection files and adds the status overlay; genres come from TMDb rather than IMDb.

nodes.label: Kapowarr ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Declares Kapowarr as a Media Management app fronted by authentik forward_single proxy, restricted to the media-managers group, with a Gatus HTTP 200 check on the app root.

nodes.label: Kometa Movie Chart Collections
nodes.rationale: Plex Popular, Trending, Popular, Top Rated and Oscars, sourced from Tautulli watch history plus Trakt/TMDb/IMDb lists.

nodes.label: Kometa TV Chart Collections
nodes.rationale: Same five-chart shape as the movie file (Plex Popular, Trending, Popular, Top Rated) but ending in Emmy Winners instead of Oscars.

nodes.label: Kometa Best-Of Collections
nodes.rationale: Decade collections from curated Trakt lists plus a parameterised Best of <<year>> template that interpolates the year into a Rotten Tomatoes Trakt list URL, so adding a year is a one-line template call.

nodes.label: Kometa Holiday Collections
nodes.rationale: Seven seasonal collections (Christmas, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Valentine's, St. Patrick's, Easter, Independence Day) built from IMDb and Trakt lists with ThePosterDB posters.

nodes.label: Kometa Network Collections
nodes.rationale: One Network template driven by TMDb network IDs; multi-ID strings (HBO, Disney+, BBC) merge a broadcaster's successor/regional network IDs into a single collection. optional: network keeps a missing network from failing the run.

nodes.label: Kometa Root Config
nodes.rationale: Binds the two Plex libraries to their collection files and wires the external services (Plex, Tautulli, TMDb, OMDb, MDBList, Radarr, Sonarr) by in-cluster service DNS with <<APIKEY>> placeholders injected from the kometa-secret env.

nodes.label: Lidarr ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Music collection manager, same Media Management category and media-managers access policy as Kapowarr; Gatus probes /ping rather than the app root.

nodes.label: Kapowarr Nightly Low-Power Maintenance Window
nodes.rationale: The service is scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly power shed (docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md), so a failed Gatus check in that 7h window is expected, not an incident. Gatus keeps checking and keeps history; it just does not alert.

nodes.label: Date-Ranged Collection Visibility
nodes.rationale: visible_home/visible_shared use range(MM/DD-MM/DD) so holiday collections are built year-round but only surface on the home row during their season — the collection stays materialised, only its visibility is scheduled.

nodes.label: Per-Value remoteRef Instead of dataFrom.extract
nodes.rationale: The nineteen-field shared/media-management-secrets blob was split (docs/openbao-shared-secrets-reorg.md §G) and Kometa wanted seven of them. Explicit data: entries remove the EMPTY-IS-NOT-MISSING hazard of dataFrom.extract: a template referencing an absent field failed the whole ExternalSecret under missingkey=error, whereas a data: entry naming a nonexistent path fails naming the path, not the template variable. tmdb_apikey was dropped from the blob rather than moved because it duplicated third-party-tokens/tmdb/api-key that xcproxy already reads — two homes for one vendor key means no way to tell which one a rotation updated.

nodes.label: Lidarr Nightly Low-Power Maintenance Window
nodes.rationale: Identical 02:00 + 7h Gatus maintenance window to Kapowarr's: the nightly power shed scales the service to 0, so failures in that window are expected and must not alert.

nodes.label: Two-Step Secret Key Rewrite
nodes.rationale: The first regexp normalises the credential Secret's hyphenated keys (public-hostname, jdbc-uri, connection-string) into legal Go template identifiers; the second prefixes postgres_. Only five plain keys are used, but normalising all of them means adding a sixth needs no thought. The keys are spelled out rather than dataFrom-ed through because Lidarr reads LIDARR__SECTION__KEY env vars whose prefix is not derivable from ${APP} — kustomize has no upper-case function.

nodes.label: PostgresHost as the Postgres On-Switch
nodes.rationale: Sonarr-family apps use Postgres if and only if PostgresHost is non-empty (NzbDrone.Core/Datastore/ConnectionStringFactory.cs). Deleting this ExternalSecret and the envFrom that reads it drops the app back onto the SQLite file still sitting in its config PVC — that is the rollback, and why the file is not deleted.

nodes.label: Servarr main/log Database Pair
nodes.rationale: Lidarr opens both ${APP} and ${APP}-log at startup and creates neither, so the log database must exist first (declared in ./postgres-databases/, rendered by components/postgres/databases). The main DB is renamed from the wiki's <app>-main because components/postgres names an app's database after the app; -log keeps the wiki name because nothing constrains it. Both share ONE credential — ConnectionStringFactory varies only the database name — so there is no second role and no second OpenBao static role. LOGDB is therefore a literal, not a Secret key.

nodes.label: API-Key Route Bypass Rule
nodes.rationale: The first HTTPRoute rule matches an X-Api-Key header or apikey query param and routes to the local-user middleware, so machine clients (other Servarr apps, Kometa) authenticate by API key while browsers fall through to the authenticated-user SSO rule.

nodes.label: Widened Startup Probe for Migration Replay
nodes.norm_label: widened startup probe for migration replay
nodes.rationale: failureThreshold went 3 -> 60 (about ten minutes). First boot against an EMPTY Postgres database replays the entire migration chain, and every 30-day password rotation forces a cold start; the old ~110s liveness budget could not cover it. A startup probe suspends both liveness and readiness until it passes and costs nothing on a normal boot.

nodes.norm_label: nightly low power shed maintenance window
nodes.rationale: These services are scaled to 0 between 02:00 and 09:00 by the nightly low-power shed (docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md). A failed Gatus check in that window is expected rather than an incident, so a maintenance-window suppresses alerting while Gatus keeps checking and keeps the history.

nodes.label: Tandoor Startup Probe Cold-Boot Window
nodes.rationale: A cold boot is nginx -> wait for DB -> migrate -> collectstatic -> gunicorn, and collectstatic re-hashes every static file on every start (~2m40s measured). Liveness only allows 40s, so without a startup probe the container is killed mid-collectstatic and crash-loops instead of converging (observed 2026-08-25 during the tranche-3 password rotation: 6 restarts, though the credential was never the problem). Liveness/readiness timeouts were also widened from 1s to 5s because a timed-out probe counts as a FAILED probe (the `499` in the access log) and three of them killed the container. A pending startup probe suppresses liveness and readiness, so this only widens the boot window and leaves steady-state behaviour untouched.

nodes.label: Tandoor Postgres Password Rotation via Reloader
nodes.norm_label: tandoor postgres password rotation via reloader
nodes.rationale: POSTGRES_PASSWORD is owned by OpenBao and rotates on a 30-day period. Preflighted in tranche 3: the Deployment carries reloader.stakater.com/auto and reads the password through envFrom on ${APP}-env, so the forced restart actually reaches the app.

nodes.label: pdm service (Proxmox Datacenter Manager container)
nodes.rationale: Runs with cgroup: host, seccomp/apparmor unconfined and cap_add ALL because the image is a systemd-based Proxmox appliance container. Its Traefik router deliberately carries NO forward-auth middleware: PDM has native OIDC support, so authentik fronting it would double-authenticate.

nodes.label: PDM ApplicationDefinition (native OIDC client)
nodes.rationale: Declares a confidential authentik oauth2 client with subMode user_email and includeClaimsInIdToken, because PDM maps identities by email rather than by opaque subject.

nodes.label: zot container registry mirror service
nodes.rationale: Publishes port 6785 directly in addition to Traefik routing, because image pulls must work even when the ingress is down; config.json is bind-mounted from the stack directory rather than templated.

nodes.label: Container Registry Mirror ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Probes /livez rather than the root URL, since a registry root returns no useful status for an unauthenticated GET.

nodes.label: PDM root password via ref+openbao
nodes.rationale: Secrets reach Dockge compose files as `ref+openbao://secrets/clusters/<key>/apps/<app>/<leaf>#/<field>` literals resolved by vals at deploy time, never as plaintext in git.

nodes.label: Dual entrypoint routing (websecure + tailscale)
nodes.rationale: Each Dockge app declares two Traefik routers over one service: `<app>.${searchDomain}` on the websecure entrypoint with the `le` certresolver, and `<app>.${tailscaleDomain}` on the tailscale entrypoint with no certresolver, so tailnet access does not depend on public ACME issuance.

nodes.label: llama-voice (llama.cpp Vulkan server, gemma-4-E2B)
nodes.rationale: E2B rather than E4B is deliberate: voice latency lives on time-to-first-token and the smaller model roughly doubles decode speed on this iGPU (~17 vs ~10 tok/s). Single slot (-np 1) and an 8192-token window keep latency down while HA's system prompt stays in the prompt cache. Port 8080 stays published because the Home Assistant voice pipeline points at ${ipAddress}:8080 and must not depend on Traefik being up. No authentik middleware — forward-auth would break API clients.

nodes.label: llama.cpp Voice Server ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Health is probed through Traefik at /health even though Home Assistant talks to ${ipAddress}:8080 directly, so the check does not gate the path HA actually depends on.

nodes.label: wyoming-piper (TTS)
nodes.rationale: CPU-only, voice en_US-lessac-medium, publishes raw TCP 10200 for Home Assistant's Wyoming integration.

nodes.label: wyoming-whisper (STT)
nodes.rationale: Runs on CPU (the iGPU is reserved for llama-voice) with model small-int8 to balance accuracy against the 8 Zen3 cores; publishes raw TCP 10300 instead of routing through Traefik because Wyoming is not HTTP.

nodes.label: Wyoming Speech ApplicationDefinition (no launch URL)
nodes.rationale: Omits `url:` on purpose: Wyoming speaks raw TCP with no web UI, and authentik validates meta_launch_url with Django's URL validator (http/https/ftp/ftps only), so a tcp:// value 400s and stalls the stack. Gatus still probes the tcp:// endpoints with [CONNECTED] == true.

nodes.label: Disable IPv6 inside container to fix -hf model downloads
nodes.norm_label: disable ipv6 inside container to fix -hf model downloads
nodes.rationale: Dockge LXCs have no IPv6 egress (ipv6_method: none) but huggingface.co resolves to AAAA records, and llama.cpp's HTTP client does not fall back to IPv4 the way curl does — every -hf download fails instantly with 'HTTPLIB failed: Could not establish connection'. net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1 forces the v4 path. Verified on celestia 2026-08-03.

nodes.label: alpha-site uses authentik's embedded outpost, not the sidecar
nodes.norm_label: alpha-site uses authentik's embedded outpost, not the sidecar
nodes.rationale: A .ignore suppresses the _common authentik-outpost sidecar on this host only; Traefik forwardAuth points at the authentik server container and local proxy providers attach to the embedded outpost. This dissolves the §2.4 bootstrap loop through createOutpost rather than sequencing around it, and returns the sidecar's ~61 MiB.

nodes.label: 07 — Authentik moves to alpha-site
nodes.rationale: Removes Kubernetes — and therefore the SGC→equestria merge — from authentik's blast radius before any node is touched. Server, worker, database and a bundled Redis move to Dockge on the Pi; in-cluster outposts stay where they are.

nodes.label: 08 — Test-target re-designation
nodes.rationale: Once piece 07 lands, CLAUDE.md's 'test risky changes against alpha-site first' reads as 'test risky changes on the box that holds identity' — not stale, actively dangerous. Ships in the same PR as 07 so the window is zero.

nodes.label: envRefs.PULUMI_BACKEND_URL instead of spec.backend
nodes.rationale: A postgres:// URL embeds the password and spec.backend is a literal string that lands in git. Reading the operator's Go source: setupWorkspace only appends PULUMI_BACKEND_URL when stack.Backend is non-empty, and SetEnvRefsForWorkspace appends envRefs afterward unconditionally — so an omitted backend plus a Secret-typed envRef lands cleanly with no duplicate. That is a source read, not a live test, which is why the one-stack smoke test is the literal first migration action.

nodes.label: The authentik stack must be host-scoped, not _common
nodes.norm_label: the authentik stack must be host-scoped, not _common
nodes.rationale: DockgeLxc.deployStacks builds each host's stack list as the union of docker/_common/* and docker/<host>/*, so a _common placement would deploy authentik to every Dockge host. It also cannot carry an `authentik:` self-provisioning block in its own definition.yaml — authentik cannot be an OAuth client of itself.

nodes.label: Preview-before-deploy safety rule
nodes.rationale: `pulumi preview` is mandatory before every `up`, and risky provider/DNS changes are rehearsed against a non-production stack (alpha-site at the time of writing) first.

nodes.norm_label: postgres-roles deliberately excluded from app kustomization

nodes.label: 2.4b — Remove the Password Rollback
nodes.rationale: disablePassword: true, delete the sops document, delete openbao-credentials.yaml, and hostnossl openbao openbao all reject — done as ONE change after a soak, because any one of them removes the ability to fall back. The soak gate was met in the sense the plan intended: the replicas cold-started on cert auth 90 minutes after the certificate was issued.

nodes.label: openbao-replica-dump Nightly pg_dump CronJob
nodes.rationale: Had to be moved onto the client certificate BEFORE disablePassword, or the failure would surface at 03:00 rather than at merge. It was authenticating with the password AND sslmode=disable, so both halves of 2.4b would have rejected it independently. pg_dump is libpq, which DOES enforce key permissions, unlike pgx.

nodes.label: passwords.sops.yaml Retirement
nodes.rationale: Phase 4's line 'delete passwords.sops.yaml' was wrong as written: each <app>-postgres-password Secret carries database/hostname/password/port/username and the OpenBao generator returns only username and password. Retiring the file needed the connection metadata REHOMED first (to <app>-postgres-conn, #1176), then the documents could go. 19 documents down to 2; every surviving document was fingerprinted before and compared after.
nodes.source_location: passwords.sops.yaml is down to two documents

nodes.label: components/postgres/rotate Folded into the Base Component
nodes.norm_label: components/postgres/rotate folded into the base component
nodes.rationale: The staging the sibling provided had done its job across nine tranches, and by then components/postgres ALONE was a broken configuration: no <app>-postgres-password document existed any more, so the base component's passwordSecret pointed at a Secret that could not exist. A new app that forgot the rotate line would silently never get a role.

nodes.label: defaultMode 0400 Lands as 0440 via fsGroup
nodes.rationale: kubelet ORs the pod's fsGroup group-read bit into the volume mode, so 0400 becomes r--r----- owned by group 1000. It does not matter for pgx, which does os.ReadFile with no permission check — but it does matter for libpq (pg_dump), and without an fsGroup the files are root-owned and unreadable by the app uid.

nodes.label: Orphaned openbao-postgres ExternalSecret Feeds the Nightly Dump
nodes.norm_label: orphaned openbao-postgres externalsecret feeds the nightly dump
nodes.rationale: The prune guard and deletionPolicy: Orphan kept the object alive but nothing in git declared it, so the next person tidying orphans would have taken the nightly openbao-replica-dump with them. The fix was to RE-DECLARE it in openbao-credentials.yaml, not to delete it.

nodes.label: Low Power Mode (Nightly Shed)
nodes.rationale: py-kube-downscaler owns replica counts in the equestria namespace, which is the shed-list namespace. Entering Low Power is `kubectl annotate namespace equestria downscaler/force-downtime=true`, scaling every non-excluded Deployment/StatefulSet to 0 and suspending CronJobs between 02:00 and 09:00. Documented in docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md.

nodes.label: Rotating Credential Restart Chain
nodes.rationale: OpenBao rotates the Postgres password every 30 days; the ExternalSecret refreshes at 4m so the new value lands before the old one is refused; the Deployment reads it via envFrom and carries reloader.stakater.com/auto, which turns the Secret change into a pod restart; the startup probe is what makes that cold restart survivable while migrations replay. Shared verbatim by bazarr and jellyseerr.

nodes.label: Bazarr ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Gatus maintenance-windows 02:00 for 7h cover the nightly Low Power shed, so a failed check while the service is scaled to 0 is expected rather than an incident - Gatus keeps checking and keeps history, it just does not alert. Authentik forward_single proxy, access limited to the media-managers group.

nodes.label: Bazarr Postgres ExternalSecret (bazarr-env)
nodes.rationale: Pulls ${APP}-postgres from the `database` ClusterSecretStore, whose password OpenBao rotates every 30 days. refreshInterval 4m matches the rotation ExternalSecret so a rotated password reaches the pod before the old one is refused; deletionPolicy Retain so a provider blip cannot empty the Secret the pod is mounting. Two rewrite steps normalise hyphenated Secret keys into legal Go template identifiers and prefix them with postgres_.

nodes.label: Bazarr HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: app-template OCIRepository chart, image ghcr.io/home-operations/bazarr 1.6.0 digest-pinned, strategy Recreate, runs as uid/gid 568 non-root. envFrom secretRef bazarr-env rather than discrete secretKeyRefs so the whole connection moves as one unit and reloader.stakater.com/auto turns a rotated Secret into a restart. Config PVC ${APP}, emptyDir cache, shared truenas-media claim, internal Gateway HTTPRoute through the traefik local-user middleware.

nodes.label: Bazarr Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: dependsOn truenas-volumes, external-secrets, postgres, volsync and tailscale-operator. Pulls the postgres, tailscale, volsync and failover/fast-node-eviction components; the postgres component provides the rotating credential that reloader turns into a restart, which the helmrelease startup probe makes survivable. See docs/runbooks/media-stack-postgres-migration.md.

nodes.label: Emby ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Media category, access limited to the friends and family groups, Gatus HTTP 200 check with no maintenance window (unlike bazarr/jellyseerr).

nodes.label: Emby HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: emby/embyserver 4.10.0.27 digest-pinned. EMBY_* env vars split config/data/cache/log dirs; DOTNET_SYSTEM_IO_DISABLEFILELOCKING is set because the .NET runtime's file locking misbehaves on the network-backed config volume. emptyDir transcode/cache/logs, config PVC, and truenas-media subPath mounts for movies and tvshows. Exposed both on the internal Gateway HTTPRoute (traefik local-user middleware) and via a tailscale Ingress, with gethomepage.dev widget annotations.

nodes.label: Emby Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: dependsOn truenas-volumes, volsync and tailscale-operator (no postgres - Emby is file-backed). VOLSYNC_CAPACITY 60Gi on the longhorn storage class.

nodes.label: Emby Kustomize Resource List
nodes.rationale: Lists only helmrelease.yaml and definition.yaml - restart.yaml is NOT included, so the emby-restart CronJob in the eris namespace is carried in the tree but not applied by this Kustomization.

nodes.label: emby-restart CronJob and RBAC
nodes.rationale: Daily 08:00 `kubectl rollout restart deployment/emby` from the eris namespace, using a dedicated ServiceAccount whose Role is scoped to resourceNames [emby] on deployments only. concurrencyPolicy Forbid, backoffLimit 2, activeDeadlineSeconds 600.

nodes.label: Jellyfin ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Access limited to the friends and family groups; Gatus HTTP 200 check with no maintenance window, consistent with Jellyfin being on the Low Power keep-list.

nodes.label: Jellyfin HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: jellyfin/jellyfin 12.0-rc3, uid/gid 568 with supplementalGroups 44/109/10000 for render/video device access. Requires an Intel iGPU: gpu.intel.com/i915 device request plus required nodeAffinity on intel.feature.node.kubernetes.io/gpu. NFS-mounted metadata, subtitles and trickplay from ${SPIKE_IP}:/mnt/stash/data/jellyfin, shared truenas-media claim, emptyDir transcode/cache/logs.

nodes.label: Jellyfin Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: dependsOn truenas-volumes, volsync and tailscale-operator; pulls failover/fast-node-eviction, tailscale and volsync components. VOLSYNC_CAPACITY 60Gi on longhorn.

nodes.label: Jellyfin Kustomize Resource List
nodes.rationale: Lists only helmrelease.yaml and definition.yaml - restart.yaml is not included, so the jellyfin-restart CronJob is carried but not applied by this Kustomization.

nodes.label: jellyfin-restart CronJob and RBAC
nodes.rationale: Daily 08:00 `kubectl rollout restart deployment/jellyfin` from the eris namespace via a dedicated ServiceAccount whose Role is scoped to resourceNames [jellyfin]. Identical in shape to emby-restart.

nodes.label: Jellyseerr ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Request management for friends and family. Gatus probes /ping and carries the 02:00 + 7h maintenance window for the nightly Low Power shed so a check failure while scaled to 0 is not an incident.

nodes.label: Jellyseerr Postgres ExternalSecret (jellyseerr-env)
nodes.rationale: Same shape as Bazarr's: extracts ${APP}-postgres from the `database` ClusterSecretStore, refreshInterval 4m to match the 30-day OpenBao rotation, deletionPolicy Retain, and the same two-step regexp rewrite into postgres_* template identifiers. CONFIG_DIRECTORY and the config PVC are unchanged because settings.json, logs and the image cache live there regardless of DB_TYPE - settings.json holds the API key and every service pairing, so a database cutover does not mean re-pairing with Plex/Jellyfin/Sonarr/Radarr.

nodes.label: Jellyseerr HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: ghcr.io/seerr-team/seerr v3.4.1 digest-pinned, strategy Recreate, uid/gid 568 non-root with no supplementalGroups. envFrom secretRef jellyseerr-env so the whole connection moves as one unit and reloader turns a rotated Secret into a restart; startup probe on /ping port 5055 with failureThreshold 60 covers the migration chain. Config PVC at /app/config, internal Gateway HTTPRoute through the traefik local-user middleware.

nodes.label: Jellyseerr Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: dependsOn truenas-volumes, external-secrets, postgres, volsync and tailscale-operator; pulls failover/fast-node-eviction, postgres, tailscale and volsync components. The postgres component supplies the rotating DB_PASS that reloader turns into a restart, which the helmrelease startup probe makes survivable. See docs/runbooks/media-stack-postgres-migration.md.

nodes.label: Low Power Drift-Detection Ignore Patch
nodes.rationale: 48 HelmReleases run driftDetection: mode: enabled, so Flux would see the downscaler's replicas: 0 as drift and correct it inside the 15m interval, partially undoing the nightly shed several times an hour. The patch injects spec.patches into every child Flux Kustomization so each HelmRelease ignores /spec/replicas (untargeted - only Deployment/StatefulSet/ReplicaSet have it) and /spec/suspend (targeted at CronJob, because Flux's own Kustomization and HelmRelease also have /spec/suspend and must not be ignored there). Applied namespace-wide rather than per-HelmRelease deliberately: a per-app opt-in would have to be remembered 60+ times and would fail silently, only during a shed window. Cost: replica drift is no longer corrected for keep-list apps - accepted because nothing but the downscaler writes replicas on these workloads. Depends on no equestria child setting spec.patches of its own.

nodes.label: Bazarr Backup Task Branches On config.yaml, Not Env
nodes.norm_label: bazarr backup task branches on config.yaml, not env
nodes.rationale: bazarr/utilities/backup.py branches on settings.postgresql.enabled - the config.yaml key, not the env var everything else honours. Enabling Postgres by environment alone leaves the backup path believing it is on SQLite; it opens a non-existent /config/db/bazarr.db and logs an exception every run. The runbook sets postgresql.enabled: true in /config/config/config.yaml once by hand during cutover. Bazarr's own backup is redundant here anyway - the database is dumped nightly by the CNPG backup CronJob.

nodes.label: Discrete Postgres Vars Instead of POSTGRES_URL
nodes.norm_label: discrete postgres vars instead of postgres_url
nodes.rationale: Bazarr 1.6.0 added POSTGRES_URL but it does not work alone: bazarr/app/database.py reads os.getenv('POSTGRES_HOST', settings.postgresql.host) and config.py gives postgresql.host a must_exist default of localhost that validate_all() always materialises. That truthy default is applied over the URL via url.set(), silently replacing host and port, so the URL renders as postgresql://bazarr:***@localhost:5432/bazarr and the pod cannot connect. Six discrete variables are used instead.

nodes.label: PGSSLCERT Points At A Nonexistent /tmp Path
nodes.norm_label: pgsslcert points at a nonexistent /tmp path
nodes.rationale: A libpq variable, not a Bazarr one, and defensive rather than functional. psycopg2 looks for a client certificate at $HOME/.postgresql/postgresql.crt; the image sets no HOME and the pod runs as uid 568, so the lookup resolves to /root/.postgresql and fails with `could not open certificate file ... Permission denied`. libpq ignores a missing cert but not an unreadable directory, so pointing PGSSLCERT at a nonexistent /tmp path is the fix. psycopg2 is not in Bazarr's base requirements - the ghcr.io/home-operations/bazarr image installs it from postgres-requirements.txt, which is why this works on that image and would not on others.

nodes.label: POSTGRES_ENABLED Must Be The String "true"
nodes.rationale: The check is POSTGRES_ENABLED_ENV.lower() == 'true', so "1", "yes" and "on" evaluate FALSE and Bazarr starts silently on the SQLite file in /config with no error. Confirm cutover from the startup log line `Connecting to PostgreSQL database: ...` rather than assuming.

nodes.label: Startup Probe Buys A Migration Window (Bazarr)
nodes.norm_label: startup probe buys a migration window (bazarr)
nodes.rationale: First boot against an EMPTY Postgres database runs the whole migration chain, and every 30-day password rotation forces a cold start. Without a startup probe the liveness budget is initialDelay + failureThreshold x period = ~110s; the kubelet kills the pod mid-migration and the restart replays it from the top. A startup probe suspends liveness AND readiness until it passes, so 60 x 10s buys ten minutes and costs nothing on a normal boot.

nodes.label: Jellyfin CPU Request Of 1 With No CPU Limit
nodes.norm_label: jellyfin cpu request of 1 with no cpu limit
nodes.rationale: The old 4-core request was sized against the wrong bottleneck: the iGPU was shared 5 ways rather than 3, so transcodes contended for GPU time and it read as a CPU shortage; observed steady state is single-digit millicores. Deliberately no cpu limit because CPU is compressible - without a ceiling the pod takes whatever the node has spare and throttles proportionally under contention rather than being capped while cores sit idle, and the request is what sets that proportional share and what the scheduler reserves. This change survived the 2026-08-22 revert of the media relocation even though the memory cut made in the same PR did not.

nodes.label: Jellyfin Low Power Keep-List Exclusion
nodes.rationale: downscaler/exclude: "true" on the controller keeps Jellyfin running through `downscaler/force-downtime` on the equestria namespace. A per-workload exclude beats the namespace toggle in py-kube-downscaler's scaler.py define_scope. See docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md.

nodes.label: Size Media Memory Limits Off Peak, Never Off Idle
nodes.norm_label: size media memory limits off peak, never off idle
nodes.rationale: The 8Gi limit was restored after being cut to 4Gi on 2026-08-22 to fit a 16GB control plane, on a steady-state reading of ~1.8Gi. That sizing was wrong: plex, cut the same way on the same reasoning, was OOMKilled that evening (exit 137, 2026-08-22T18:52:15Z), and Prometheus max_over_time(container_memory_working_set_bytes[6h]) put a jellyfin pod at 2.62 GiB - two thirds of a 4Gi ceiling before a library scan. Unlike CPU, memory is not compressible, so an undersized limit OOMKills.

nodes.label: DB_NAME Set Explicitly Rather Than Relying On The Code Default
nodes.norm_label: db_name set explicitly rather than relying on the code default
nodes.rationale: The code default (jellyseerr) already matches, but components/postgres owns that name; an app that silently depended on a hard-coded default matching a component's naming convention would be a trap the first time either side changed.

nodes.label: DB_TYPE Must Be Exactly "postgres"
nodes.rationale: server/datasource.ts is `export const isPgsql = process.env.DB_TYPE === 'postgres'` - a strict, case-sensitive comparison with no validation and no warning. "postgresql", "Postgres" or a missing value all select SQLite silently and the app comes up looking healthy on an empty local database. Verify after cutover by querying Postgres, not by loading the UI.

nodes.label: Do Not Override The Jellyseerr Container Command
nodes.norm_label: do not override the jellyseerr container command
nodes.rationale: Migrations run at boot only when NODE_ENV === 'production', and nothing in the image environment sets it - it comes from the `start` script (NODE_ENV=production node dist/index.js) that the default `pnpm start` command invokes. Replacing command:/args: without carrying NODE_ENV forward gives a pod that connects to Postgres and then skips its migrations.

nodes.label: Startup Probe Buys A Migration Window (Jellyseerr)
nodes.norm_label: startup probe buys a migration window (jellyseerr)
nodes.rationale: First boot against an EMPTY Postgres database runs the whole migration chain, and every 30-day password rotation forces a cold start. Without a startup probe the liveness budget is initialDelay + failureThreshold x period = ~110s; the kubelet kills the pod mid-migration and the restart replays it from the top. A startup probe suspends liveness AND readiness until it passes, so 60 x 10s buys ten minutes and costs nothing on a normal boot.

nodes.norm_label: traefik entrypoints (web, websecure, tailscale, sftp, metrics, bolt)

nodes.norm_label: traefik prometheus metrics on the metrics entrypoint

nodes.label: Mediated Docker socket access over TCP 2375
nodes.norm_label: mediated docker socket access over tcp 2375

nodes.label: arcane (Docker manager) container
nodes.rationale: Reaches Docker through DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375 rather than a bind-mounted /var/run/docker.sock, so the socket is mediated. Port 3552 behind Traefik on websecure + tailscale, with an oidc-mapping.json mounted read-only.

nodes.label: Docker access via docker-socket-proxy
nodes.rationale: Container management surfaces talk to a TCP socket proxy on dockge_default instead of the raw docker socket, so the reachable API surface is filtered rather than root-equivalent.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Arcane
nodes.rationale: Confidential authentik OAuth2 client with two redirect URIs (web callback plus an arcane-mobile:// deep link) and a custom arcane_groups property mapping so Arcane can do group-based authorization from the ID token. subMode user_email.

nodes.label: No docker socket, no host bind mounts
nodes.norm_label: no docker socket, no host bind mounts
nodes.rationale: The image ships docker-cli and Hermes has a docker terminal backend, so mounting the socket would hand the agent control of every container on celestia including its own. Same reasoning bars /opt/stacks: the agent must not be able to rewrite the compose files that constrain it.

nodes.label: Estate bar for routing high-blast-radius apps on websecure
nodes.norm_label: estate bar for routing high-blast-radius apps on websecure
nodes.rationale: Hermes is routed on websecure like arcane (which controls Docker) and pdm (which controls Proxmox). Those are comparable or greater blast radius behind the same authentik gate, so this is the estate's existing bar rather than a loosening of it — and the gate is genuinely enforced because the dashboard refuses to serve a single protected route without a completed OIDC login.

nodes.label: CONNECT_HOST repoint from op-connect.sgc to op-connect.equestria
nodes.norm_label: connect_host repoint from op-connect.sgc to op-connect.equestria
nodes.rationale: A two-line change in two repos' .config/mise.toml. It still matters because nine call sites still construct live OnePasswordItem writes, so Connect reachability is load-bearing for more than a human LXC login — but it is now a write-path concern only, not a read dependency.

nodes.label: OIDC auth method moved from equestria-init.sh into components/openbao/oidc.ts
nodes.norm_label: oidc auth method moved from equestria-init.sh into components/openbao/oidc.ts
nodes.rationale: The viewer policy, the oidc JWT auth backend and the admin/family roles became vault.Policy / vault.jwt.AuthBackend(Role) wired into stacks/home. The real win is that the Authentik client credentials produced by the applications stack are read directly by Pulumi instead of a human copying client_id/secret/issuer into env vars for a one-shot script.

nodes.label: 03 — Secrets bootstrap independence
nodes.rationale: Goal: a local pulumi preview succeeds from a laptop with both clusters powered off. The framing inverted since the issue was opened — the catch-22 is now OpenBao-shaped, not 1Password-shaped.

nodes.label: The bootstrap dividing line (what can never become a Pulumi resource)
nodes.norm_label: the bootstrap dividing line (what can never become a pulumi resource)
nodes.rationale: Pulumi authenticates to OpenBao with a token, so anything required to make that token exist (operator init, recovery-share handling, root-token regeneration, the pulumi AppRole) cannot be a Pulumi resource — it would be a resource in the system it is bootstrapping. Everything after the first working token is fair game.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: grafana-operator
nodes.rationale: wait: true (unlike blackbox-exporter) because the dashboards Kustomization needs the operator's CRDs established first; deletionPolicy: Orphan per the migration-churn runbook.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: grafana-operator
nodes.rationale: grafana-operator 5.25.0 with driftDetection enabled; reconciles every GrafanaFolder and GrafanaDashboard CR in this namespace into the Grafana instance selected by dashboards=grafana.

nodes.label: Tier 1 control-plane toleration (low-power tier)
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 per docs/cluster-consolidation/24 §1: the observability namespace must stay up during Battery mode, so its workloads tolerate node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule and can land on the control-plane nodes that stay powered. Path verified against the chart; added after §8 Stage 2. See docs/cluster-consolidation/20-low-power-tier.md §4.

nodes.label: GrafanaDashboard: blackbox-exporter (grafana.com 7587)
nodes.rationale: Renders the probe_* series produced by the blackbox-exporter HelmRelease's ServiceMonitor.

nodes.norm_label: garage-system exclusion after fail-closed pvc webhook outage

nodes.label: Downscaler opt-out scope vs inert action polarity
nodes.norm_label: downscaler opt-out scope vs inert action polarity

nodes.label: Shared npm cache hostPath (/var/lib/pulumi-npm-cache)
nodes.rationale: Node-local hostPath mounted at /root/.npm in every workspace pod so repeated `npm ci` runs do not re-download the workspace dependency tree.

nodes.label: Alert: PulumiStackFailed
nodes.rationale: Keys off lastUpdate.failures rather than a condition type because the counter increments on every failed run and therefore covers both `failed` and `retryingAfterFailure` states.

nodes.label: Alert: PulumiStackLocked
nodes.rationale: Matches 'locked by' in status.lastUpdate.message. Documented as self-healing via the auto-canceller CronJob, with a manual `kubectl exec ... pulumi cancel --yes` escape hatch in the annotation.

nodes.label: Alert: PulumiStackPrerequisiteNotSatisfied
nodes.rationale: Watches the Reconciling condition with reason=PrerequisiteNotSatisfied, which is how a Stack reports that a `prerequisites:` entry has not succeeded.

nodes.label: Alert: PulumiStackStalled
nodes.rationale: Separates 'failing' from 'cannot make progress' with a much higher failure threshold (>100 for 30m).

nodes.label: ExternalName Service: equestria-kubeproxy
nodes.rationale: Routes pulumi workspace pods to the equestria Kubernetes API server over the tailnet-inbound egress ProxyGroup instead of exposing the API server directly.

nodes.label: ExternalName Service: sgc-kubeproxy
nodes.rationale: Same tailnet-egress pattern as equestria-kubeproxy, giving workspace pods reach into the SGC cluster API server.

nodes.label: CronJob: pulumi-lock-canceller
nodes.rationale: Runs every 5 minutes and cancels Pulumi state locks older than 10 minutes by exec'ing `pulumi cancel` in the stack's `<stack>-workspace-0` pod. Stale locks are left behind when a workspace pod restarts mid-run; without this the stack blocks indefinitely. Substitution is disabled on the manifest so the shell script's ${...} expansions survive Flux postBuild.

nodes.label: ClusterRole: pulumi-lock-canceller (get/list stacks)
nodes.rationale: Cluster-wide read on pulumi.com/stacks because the canceller scans stacks in every namespace; write access is deliberately withheld since cancelling happens via pod exec, not the CR.

nodes.label: Role: pulumi-lock-canceller (pods, pods/exec)
nodes.rationale: pods/exec create is namespace-scoped to pulumi so the canceller can only exec into workspace pods in its own namespace.

nodes.label: CronJob: pulumi-npm-cache-prune
nodes.rationale: Weekly per-node prune of the shared /var/lib/pulumi-npm-cache hostPath. Uses completions/parallelism=4 plus a hostname topology spread so exactly one pod lands on each node — the cache is node-local, so a single pod would only ever prune one node's copy. Node-count changes require editing completions.

nodes.label: ClusterRole: kube-state-metrics-pulumi-stacks
nodes.rationale: kube-state-metrics needs list/watch on pulumi.com/stacks for the customResourceState metrics kube_stack_status_condition, kube_stack_last_update_failures and kube_stack_last_update_state; without this grant every Pulumi alert silently never fires.

nodes.label: kustomize overlay: operator helmrelease + rules + rbac
nodes.norm_label: kustomize overlay: operator helmrelease + rules + rbac

nodes.label: NODE_OPTIONS heap cap under the container limit
nodes.norm_label: node_options heap cap under the container limit
nodes.rationale: --max-old-space-size=4096 sits well under the 6Gi container limit so V8 proactively GCs instead of ballooning until the kernel OOM-kills the whole process tree.

nodes.label: OpenBao dual-write env wiring (BAO_ADDR/ROLE_ID/SECRET_ID)
nodes.rationale: Without all three vars GlobalResources.baoDualWriteEnabled is false and every dual-write is silently skipped while the run still reports success. They are set on EVERY stack, not only the ones that dual-write today: the provider getter is lazy, so they are inert for stacks that never touch OpenBao, and the next stack to grow a dual-write site just works. Points at openbao-active, not openbao, because the general Service also routes to standbys which answer with a 307 redirect to the leader.

nodes.label: vals initContainer (ref+openbao:// resolver)
nodes.rationale: mise fetches the vals binary so the version pin stays in the mise ecosystem (keep in step with .config/mise.toml [tools]); Kubernetes `command:` deliberately replaces the image's mise entrypoint. The install dir is a pod-local emptyDir and only the download cache is shared, because the extract is cheap and the download is not. The init runs as root: the workspace pod template pins runAsUser 1000/runAsNonRoot, under which the root-owned hostPath cache is unwritable — every early EACCES was this, not an install race. Retries the install 3x before failing.

nodes.label: OpenBao dual-write env wiring (ocracoke)
nodes.rationale: Identical uniform wiring as the other stacks; inert unless the stack actually builds the OpenBao provider.

nodes.label: Operator-only control-plane toleration (Tier 1 power state)
nodes.rationale: The control-plane toleration is applied to the operator alone, on purpose. Workspace pods come from each Stack's spec.workspaceTemplate and are left untolerated so a Battery window sheds ~1.1 GiB of long-lived workspace requests; a `pulumi up` cannot usefully run mid-outage anyway because its state backend lives off-cluster. Per docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md §1 and 20-low-power-tier.md §4.

nodes.norm_label: http_2xx_insecure module for self-signed proxmox uis

nodes.label: scripts/bao-reorg/plan.ts is the executable decision of record
nodes.norm_label: scripts/bao-reorg/plan.ts is the executable decision of record
nodes.rationale: The worksheet stays as the RATIONALE; plan.ts (146 entries, one per live path) is the executable form, and where they disagree plan.ts is what runs.

nodes.label: OpenBao secrets/shared/* reorganisation worksheet
nodes.rationale: 146 live paths, only 69 referenced anywhere in the repo; 77 are unreferenced version-1 leftovers of the op-to-bao migration. Draining shared/ is mostly a deletion job, not a move job — and deleting the dead half first is the lowest-risk work in the document.

nodes.label: The flat shared/<slug(title)> default that produced today's layout
nodes.norm_label: the flat shared/<slug(title)> default that produced today's layout
nodes.rationale: openbao-migration PLAN §A specified a nested layout, but op-to-bao's default rule (shared/<slug(title)>, flat) shipped instead because mapping.yaml was reviewed for collisions rather than for grouping. The reorg finishes Phase 4's intended layout rather than inventing a new one — so the nesting needs no new estate decision.

nodes.label: Trailing * in an OpenBao ACL is a prefix glob (nesting is free)
nodes.norm_label: trailing * in an openbao acl is a prefix glob (nesting is free)
nodes.rationale: `path "secrets/data/shared/*"` matches across `/`, so arbitrarily deep nesting under shared/ needs no policy change. A brand-new TOP-LEVEL prefix would need a grant in every eso-* policy plus the AppRole — an admin write, therefore a root ceremony. That asymmetry is the main reason to nest rather than invent prefixes.

nodes.norm_label: control-plane toleration kustomize patch for flux controllers

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: observability-priority-class
nodes.rationale: deletionPolicy: Orphan is set deliberately across the observability apps so that a Kustomization removed during cluster-consolidation churn does not delete live objects; see docs/cluster-consolidation/27-migration-churn-failure-modes.md.

nodes.label: PriorityClass: observability-critical
nodes.rationale: Value 1000 with preemptionPolicy PreemptLowerPriority and globalDefault false, so the critical observability stack (Prometheus, AlertManager, Thanos, Loki, Alloy) evicts ordinary workloads under node pressure rather than being evicted itself; scoped opt-in so nothing inherits it by accident.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Prometheus
nodes.rationale: Single driscoll.dev/v1 ApplicationDefinition drives three downstream consumers at once — dashboard entry, Authentik forward_single proxy provider, and a Gatus HTTP health check — so identity, uptime and catalog metadata cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: prometheus (kube-prometheus-stack)
nodes.rationale: Values are supplied via valuesFrom a ConfigMap rather than inline, which is what makes the reloader.stakater.com/auto annotation on the Prometheus object meaningful; install retries are unbounded (-1) while upgrade retries are capped at 3 with cleanupOnFail.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: prometheus
nodes.rationale: wait: false because the StatefulSet with a Longhorn PVC can take longer than the timeout to become ready; dependsOn spans observability-repositories, volsync, onepassword-connect and external-secrets so the chart source and the secret plumbing exist before the release is attempted.

nodes.label: configMapGenerator: prometheus-values
nodes.rationale: disableNameSuffixHash: true keeps the ConfigMap name stable so the HelmRelease valuesFrom reference does not have to change on every edit; change detection is delegated to Reloader instead of to a hashed name.

nodes.label: PrometheusRule: amd-gpu-rules
nodes.rationale: Lives in the prometheus app directory rather than its own app because the AMD half of vault#110 is a node-exporter collector flag (--collector.drm in this directory's values.yaml), not a separate workload.

nodes.label: Alert: AmdGpuMetricsAbsent
nodes.rationale: Absence-based rather than threshold-based: no utilisation baseline exists for these integrated parts, and the failure mode worth catching is silent — a kernel bump changing the sysfs layout, or --collector.drm being lost when the chart's extraArgs default list is overwritten, leaves node-exporter scraping green while node_drm_* simply stops.

nodes.label: kube-state-metrics CustomResourceState for Pulumi Stack
nodes.rationale: Exports pulumi.com/v1 Stack status as kube_stack_* gauges (status_condition, last_update_failures, last_update_state) plus a last_update_info Info metric carrying the message label, explicitly for lock detection — turning a CRD-only failure mode into something alertable.

nodes.label: node-exporter extraArgs (filesystem excludes + --collector.drm)
nodes.rationale: Helm replaces lists rather than merging them, so the two --collector.filesystem.* entries must be repeated verbatim from kube-prometheus-stack's own values.yaml — dropping them would un-exclude every container mount point and blow up filesystem-metric cardinality. --collector.drm was verified 2026-08-01 to be populated on hard-hat (0x15bf RDNA3 Phoenix) and shining-armor (0x164e RDNA2 Raphael), so it is not a silent no-op; cost is ~8 series x 2 cards. amdgpu is the only driver publishing utilisation through DRM sysfs — i915 does not, and is covered by intel-gpu-exporter (vault#110).

nodes.label: prometheusSpec values (retention, OTLP, remoteWrite)
nodes.rationale: Local retention is deliberately tiny (1d / 16GB on a 20Gi Longhorn PVC) because durable storage is Thanos Receive; the local TSDB is only a write-ahead buffer. Out-of-order window of 30m plus an OTLP receiver make it safe to accept late and push-based samples.

nodes.label: Thanos Receive remoteWrite target
nodes.rationale: writeRelabelConfigs normalise the instance label: pod name wins for pod-level metrics, node name is used only when pod is empty, so a single instance label is meaningful across both series families in the multi-cluster Thanos store.

nodes.label: Alert: VolumeSnapshotContentsGrowing
nodes.rationale: Written after vault#123 (longhorn-snapclass defaulting to deletionPolicy: Retain leaked 5,532 dangling VolumeSnapshotContents, noticed via apiserver memory pressure rather than any metric) and vault#134 (the bulk cleanup, which stalled 10 days unnoticed). Alerts on sustained growth over 7 days rather than a fixed object count so a legitimate one-off batch does not false-positive; #123's fix only stops that one leak, while any future VolumeSnapshotClass with deletionPolicy: Retain would recreate the problem silently.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: observability-repositories
nodes.rationale: Holds only sources shared by more than one app in the namespace (same shape as gha-repositories in github-actions); anything used by exactly one app stays inline in that app's helmrelease.yaml. Deliberately NOT named `observability`: a nested Kustomization sharing its namespace's name collides with the umbrella pointer Kustomization and self-prunes.

nodes.label: OCIRepository: kube-prometheus-stack
nodes.rationale: Consolidated to ONE declaration consumed by alertmanager, grafana and prometheus. It used to be copy-pasted into all three HelmReleases — three documents with the same name in the same namespace, so three Kustomizations writing one object; they only stayed stable because they were byte-identical, and any drift would have made the object flip-flop on whichever reconciled last. The duplication also produced Renovate's 'Excess registryUrls found for datasource lookup' warning (the flux manager resolves sourceRef by name+namespace across the whole repo), which is why renovate.json5 used to suppress dependencyLookupWarnings wholesale and thereby hid every genuine lookup failure.

nodes.label: OCIRepository: silence-operator
nodes.rationale: Declared inline rather than in repositories/ because it is used by exactly one app, matching the split documented in repositories/ks.yaml. Sourced from the home-operations charts-mirror rather than upstream Giant Swarm.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: silence-operator
nodes.rationale: crds: CreateReplace on both install and upgrade because the Silence CRD it owns must track the chart; image is pinned to quay.io/giantswarm/silence-operator 0.18.0 independently of the 0.20.0 chart tag. Stateless Deployment, so the control-plane toleration is placement flexibility only.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: silence-operator
nodes.rationale: dependsOn alertmanager because the operator's only job is writing silences into the Alertmanager API; a healthCheck on the HelmRelease plus wait: true means Silence CRs are only applied once the operator is actually Ready.

nodes.label: Silence: keda-hpa-maxed-out
nodes.rationale: Declarative, version-controlled silence rather than a hand-clicked one in the Alertmanager UI: KubeHpaMaxedOut is expected for every keda-hpa-* HPA (KEDA pins maxReplicas as its scaling mechanism), so the regex matcher suppresses the whole family permanently instead of expiring.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: smartctl-exporter
nodes.rationale: prometheusRules.enabled is false so the chart's bundled rules are replaced by the hand-curated set in this directory's prometheusrule.yaml; the ServiceMonitor relabels __meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name onto instance so drive alerts name the physical node rather than a pod IP.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: smartctl-exporter
nodes.rationale: dependsOn prometheus because the app ships a PrometheusRule and a ServiceMonitor, which require the operator's CRDs to exist first. Unlike its siblings it does not set deletionPolicy: Orphan — it owns no persistent state worth preserving through migration churn.

nodes.label: PrometheusRule: smartctl-exporter-rules
nodes.rationale: Hand-maintained replacement for the chart's disabled bundled rules; the last three alerts are transcribed from the upstream prometheus-community rules.txt so the local copy stays comparable to upstream when bumping.

nodes.label: Control-plane tolerations for the observability tier
nodes.norm_label: control-plane tolerations for the observability tier
nodes.rationale: REVISED 2026-08-23. kube-state-metrics and the Prometheus operator were previously left untolerated on the grounds that stateless Deployments are 'fine on the workers' — true in Full and Low Power, false in Battery where there are no workers. §8 Stage 2 proved the general form of the mistake by leaving home-assistant Pending on a cordoned cluster, so both now carry the control-plane toleration. For the Prometheus StatefulSet itself a toleration only widens where it MAY schedule; the Longhorn PVC still pins the pod to its data.

nodes.label: Proposed order — smallest blast radius first
nodes.norm_label: proposed order — smallest blast radius first

nodes.label: Environment Variables Instead of config.xml
nodes.rationale: The password rotates every 30 days and a value baked into a file on the config PVC cannot follow it. ConfigFileProvider gives the environment precedence with persist: false, so nothing is written back and the file on the PVC stays SQLite-shaped and inert — which is exactly what makes rollback a rollback rather than a restore. Sonarr alone has no connection-string option, so five discrete variables beat one variable that works on three.

nodes.label: Servarr Second Log Database
nodes.rationale: LOG__DBENABLED selects AddDummyLogDatabase() over AddLogDatabase() in Bootstrap.cs; flipping it to True makes <app>-log a HARD startup dependency the app opens at boot and will not create. One credential covers both because ConnectionStringFactory varies only the database name, nothing is migrated into it (it starts empty), and it is excluded from backup by driscoll.dev/backup: false since TrimLogDatabase prunes it anyway.
nodes.source_location: 1.1 Two databases per app, and the log one is new

nodes.label: Empty PostgresHost Rollback to SQLite
nodes.rationale: The SQLite file is untouched throughout, so rollback is just making the app stop reading the Postgres environment. An empty PostgresHost makes ConnectionStringFactory choose the SQLite path for BOTH connections, so the log database stops being needed at the same moment. What you lose is whatever was written to Postgres after cutover — say that out loud before choosing it.

nodes.label: GOMEMLIMIT and Container Limit Must Move Together
nodes.norm_label: gomemlimit and container limit must move together
nodes.rationale: The chart's 128Mi/GOMEMLIMIT=110MiB OOMKilled this operator 23 times in a row. GOMEMLIMIT is a soft ceiling on the Go HEAP only — it does not cover goroutine stacks, runtime overhead, or above all the informer caches, which is where the memory goes because rbac.scope: cluster makes every one of ~20 controllers cache its kind across ALL namespaces. Raising only the container limit leaves Go targeting a 110MiB heap and collecting too aggressively; raising only GOMEMLIMIT walks back into the OOM.

nodes.label: rbac.scope cluster and Its Bargain
nodes.rationale: The ClusterRole carries create/update/delete on Deployments, StatefulSets, Services, Secrets, ConfigMaps, ServiceAccounts, Roles and RoleBindings bound cluster-wide, so 'may create an MCPServer in namespace X' is effectively 'may run a pod, and mint RBAC for it, in namespace X'. Same bargain as CNPG, Garage and external-secrets, and it holds for the same reason: writing an MCPServer means writing to this Git repo. allowedNamespaces is NOT the lever to narrow it — that only applies under scope: namespace, and switching costs the StorageVersionMigrator.

nodes.label: storageVersionMigrator Feature
nodes.rationale: Only possible because scope is cluster — the chart's validate-features.yaml fails the render outright for any other combination, since this controller watches cluster-scoped CRDs and re-stores objects across every namespace. It keeps status.storedVersions trimmed to what is live, so a future release dropping a deprecated API version cannot orphan objects still stored under the old one. Without it that cleanup is manual, must happen BEFORE such a release lands, and nothing in-cluster warns you.

nodes.norm_label: internal gateway + local-user middleware route convention

nodes.label: iptv-sync Large-File GC Resource Sizing
nodes.rationale: The sync job requests 2 CPU / 1Gi but is allowed to burst to 8Gi memory because the playlist/EPG files it processes are large and are garbage-collected immediately; the CPU limit is deliberately left unset (commented out) so the burst is not throttled.

nodes.label: kptv-fast Startup Cache and EPG Warming
nodes.norm_label: kptv-fast startup cache and epg warming
nodes.rationale: CACHE_DURATION 86400 with WARM_CACHE_ON_STARTUP/WARM_EPG_ON_STARTUP and a 10s STARTUP_CACHE_DELAY trades a slow first boot for cheap steady-state reads; the /status probe has a 10s initial delay and 5 failures allowed so the warm-up does not trip liveness. Providers are limited to MAX_WORKERS 5 with a 60s PROVIDER_TIMEOUT and country lists scoped to us/ca/uk to bound upstream fan-out.

nodes.label: Parked pvr Apps (commented-out ks entries)
nodes.rationale: ersatztv, fhdhr, iptv-sync, nextpvr, threadfin and strmgen are commented out rather than deleted in the pvr group kustomization, so their directories stay in git but Flux never reconciles them. Re-enabling a line is not a no-op: for apps that carried a postgres component the database and login role were dropped, so the Pulumi system stack fails until CNPG recreates the role.

nodes.label: strmgen Dropped-App Postgres Order of Operations
nodes.norm_label: strmgen dropped-app postgres order of operations
nodes.rationale: The postgres component line is commented out, not deleted, because the whole ks.yaml is parked. strmgen was dropped in group E on 2026-08-25 and its Database CR, database and role were removed, so re-enabling the component does not restore the old state: the Pulumi system stack discovers the component and creates database/static-roles/${APP}, which fails outright until CNPG has recreated the login role (see components/postgres/ks.yaml).

nodes.label: Teamarr Gatus Low-Power Maintenance Window
nodes.rationale: Teamarr is scaled to 0 by the nightly Low Power shed (docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md), so a Gatus failure between 02:00 and 09:00 is expected rather than an incident. A 7h maintenance-window starting at 02:00 keeps the check running and keeps history while suppressing alerts, instead of deleting the check.

nodes.label: OpenBao Path Migration of xcproxy Secrets
nodes.norm_label: openbao path migration of xcproxy secrets
nodes.rationale: The dataFrom keys carry `# was:` comments recording the move from flat 1Password item names (XCProxy, TMDB API Key) to hierarchical OpenBao paths (clusters/equestria/apps/xcproxy/credentials, third-party-tokens/tmdb/api-key). Each extract is namespaced with a regexp rewrite prefix (xcproxy_, tmdb_) so two stores can be merged into one templated Secret without key collisions.

nodes.label: xcproxy dotnet run Single-File App Pattern
nodes.norm_label: xcproxy dotnet run single-file app pattern
nodes.rationale: Instead of building an image, xcproxy runs the .NET SDK image and executes `dotnet run /scripts/App.cs`, where App.cs is mounted from the kustomize-generated xcproxy-app-script ConfigMap. This keeps the whole application editable as source in git, at the cost of an SDK-sized image, a writable /.dotnet emptyDir, and compile-on-start latency.

nodes.label: xcproxy Downscaler Keep-List Exclusion
nodes.rationale: The controller carries `downscaler/exclude: "true"` so it survives `downscaler/force-downtime` on the equestria namespace: the per-workload exclude beats the namespace toggle in scaler.py define_scope (docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md). This is the inverse choice from teamarr, which is allowed to shed and instead suppresses alerting with a Gatus maintenance window.

nodes.label: xcproxy TMDb Enrichment and Stream De-duplication Policy
nodes.norm_label: xcproxy tmdb enrichment and stream de-duplication policy
nodes.rationale: POSTER_PREFERENCE=tmdb with TMDB_ON_LIST=false enriches details per-title but skips TMDb on list rendering to reduce timeouts and load; DEDUPE keeps one variant per title/episode ranked by PREF_QUALITY (2160p..480p) then PREF_SOURCE (remux..other). STREAM_MODE=redirect avoids proxying bytes through the pod, and a 4h CACHE_TTL bounds upstream refresh.
