nodes.norm_label: forgejo still exports the gitea_ metric namespace

nodes.label: OCIRepository app-template
nodes.rationale: Pulls the bjw-s app-template Helm chart from oci://ghcr.io/bjw-s-labs/helm/app-template at tag 5.1.0 pinned by digest, selecting the CNCF Helm chart content layer. Digest pinning makes the chart version reproducible independent of the mutable tag.

nodes.label: Coder ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: Declares the estate-facing identity of Coder: url https://code.${ROOT_DOMAIN}, the Authentik confidential OAuth2 client with two redirect URIs (public + tailnet), and a Gatus /healthz check. access_policy restricts sign-in to admins+family because Coder OSS has no IdP role sync, so Authentik decides WHO may sign in at all and every login lands as a plain Coder member; admins are promoted in-app.

nodes.label: coder-oidc-secret ExternalSecret
nodes.rationale: Reads issuer/client_id/client_secret from OpenBao at clusters/equestria/apps/coder/oidc. Moved off ClusterSecretStore/cluster because that store has remoteNamespace: equestria and Coder lives in its own coder namespace, so the source Secret was never visible and the ExternalSecret was SecretSyncedError since 2026-08-08, breaking OIDC login. OpenBao is namespace-independent by construction, so it is a fix rather than a workaround.

nodes.label: coder-pguser-secret ExternalSecret
nodes.rationale: Pulls the rotating postgres credential from ClusterSecretStore/database and renders it as a single connection URI key. Coder consumes a URI rather than a bare password, so the rotated value must arrive already embedded; the pgsql-user-template builds all keys from whichever password the ExternalSecret resolved.

nodes.label: coder HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: Upstream coder chart (not app-template). TLS is terminated by Traefik on the internal Gateway so the pod serves plain HTTP and coder.tls.*/CODER_TLS_* must not be set. Failover tolerations are written natively under coder.tolerations because the app-template-only failover component patches defaultPodOptions. CODER_DISABLE_PASSWORD_AUTH=true makes Authentik the only identity source; Prometheus is enabled with agent stats.
nodes.source_location: kind: HelmRelease name coder, chart coder 2.36.3

nodes.label: coder HTTPRoute (code.${ROOT_DOMAIN})
nodes.rationale: Primary dashboard route on the internal Gateway with the local-user Traefik middleware (internal-network guard plus error pages).

nodes.label: coder-apps HTTPRoute (*.code.${ROOT_DOMAIN})
nodes.rationale: Wildcard route for per-workspace app subdomains (dashboard port forwarding, coder_apps). Uses local-api rather than local-user because these proxy websockets and stream non-200 responses, which the error-pages middleware in local-user would break; local-api keeps the internal-network guard.

nodes.label: coder Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Depends on postgres/database and external-secrets/kube-system. Deliberately omits the failover/fast-node-eviction component because it patches defaultPodOptions which only app-template reads. Uses components/postgres rotation: Coder has no liveness probe so it cannot be probe-killed mid-boot, and it holds a connection pool so it takes a short burst of auth failures at each rotation (the rotate-then-propagate gap, not a fault).
nodes.source_location: kind: Kustomization name coder namespace coder

nodes.label: coder PodMonitor
nodes.rationale: Scrapes CODER_PROMETHEUS_ADDRESS (default 0.0.0.0:2112), which the chart does not declare as a named container port.

nodes.label: coder.rules PrometheusRule
nodes.rationale: Three alerts: CoderAbsent (absent(up{job=~'.*coder.*'}==1), critical), CoderWorkspaceBuildFailures (coderd_workspace_builds_total{status='failed'} increase over 1h), CoderAgentsUnhealthy (coderd_agents_connections in start_timeout/start_error).

nodes.label: forgejo GarageBucket
nodes.rationale: ONE bucket for every Forgejo subsystem because Forgejo's [storage] default already namespaces lfs/, packages/, attachments/, actions_artifacts/ into prefixes; a bucket per subsystem would only add eight credential sets to rotate. Carries driscoll.dev/backup=true because moving storage to S3 takes those objects off the volsync-backed PVC and they would otherwise silently stop being backed up. deletionPolicy Retain so a Flux prune orphans rather than destroys.

nodes.label: forgejo-garage-backup GarageKey (read-only)
nodes.rationale: kubernetes-backups.ts looks up backup credentials by the namespace of the bucket's clusterRef, so a Garage cluster in coder needs its own labelled Secret (driscoll.dev/garage-backup-credentials=true) — Pulumi selects on that label, not the name. allBuckets read-only: a backup identity that can mutate its source is a backup that can destroy it. additionalData.external-endpoint overrides the useless in-cluster Service URL the operator writes, because backrest runs on celestia.

nodes.label: forgejo GarageKey
nodes.rationale: createBucket false: Forgejo's minio driver calls MakeBucket on startup and falls back to BucketExists, so the denial is expected and harmless — no reason to let the forge create buckets. Secret ${APP}-forgejo-credentials includes endpoint, region and bucket name.

nodes.label: renovate GarageKey
nodes.rationale: One key serves both the renovate-operator's log store and every Renovate Job's repository cache (forwarded via S3_CREDENTIALS_SECRET_NAME). Key names access-key-id / secret-access-key are what the operator writes by default and what the chart's s3.existingSecret reads — must not be templated.

nodes.label: renovate GarageBucket
nodes.rationale: A second bucket rather than a prefix in forgejo, because forgejo carries driscoll.dev/backup=true and everything here is rebuildable; sharing would mean nightly-backing-up disposable data or maintaining another backup-exclude glob. Deliberately unannotated (not backed up). Bounded in size because both prefixes are keyed by identity, not time — renovate-logs/<ns>/<job>/<org>/<repo>.log and one cache object per repo, so each run overwrites the last.

nodes.label: Forgejo Object Storage ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: No url: and no authentik: block — there is no web UI and the S3 endpoint must never sit behind forward-auth. The Gatus check accepts 200/400/403 because an unsigned GET / is a ListBuckets Garage rejects, and that rejection proves route+TLS+endpoints+process; tightening to one code would stop catching the 503 a gateway with no backends returns.

nodes.label: forgejo-garage-secrets ExternalSecret (RPC secret + admin token)
nodes.rationale: The two identity values that must not be operator-generated: the RPC secret IS the node's mesh identity and GarageKey material derives from it, so losing it means the object store cannot be reassembled from its PVCs. Filed under the forgejo app prefix with garage- names because this cluster is not a service in its own right. Deliberately not garage-system's paths — two independent clusters must never share an RPC secret or a node could join the wrong mesh. Uses one remoteRef per value so a missing path fails naming the path, not a template variable.

nodes.label: forgejo-garage GarageCluster
nodes.rationale: Single-node, factor 1, zone coder. No image: because the operator carries a tested digest per release and the repo's customManager updates tags but not @sha256 digests. Changing the replication factor later is destructive (full layout rebuild via status.factorMigration). s3Api.region equestria is baked into every SigV4 signature, so changing it invalidates every client at once. webApi disabled; /metrics left open to the pod network so Prometheus can scrape without RBAC on this namespace's secrets. Worker tranquility is gentle so a scrub on control-plane SATA is not felt by etcd.

nodes.label: forgejo-garage-s3 HTTPRoute (s3.git.${ROOT_DOMAIN})
nodes.rationale: Exists for exactly one client: backrest on celestia, which cannot resolve a ClusterIP. Forgejo itself talks to the in-namespace Service directly to avoid a Traefik hairpin per LFS object. Deliberately NOT behind authentik forward-auth because SigV4 clients cannot follow an interactive redirect — access control is the GarageKey grant. Admin (3903) and RPC (3901) stay on the ClusterIP Service. The hostname is two labels deep so *.${ROOT_DOMAIN} does not cover it; the matching SAN is *.git.${ROOT_DOMAIN}. Path-style addressing only.

nodes.label: forgejo-garage Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Depends on the cluster-scoped garage-operator (watchNamespaces: []) and external-secrets. wait: true and forgejo dependsOn this, because Forgejo's init containers reach S3 on startup and would crash-loop until the bucket and key exist.

nodes.label: forgejo-runner-config ExternalSecret
nodes.rationale: Renders the runner config by templating the generated ConfigMap's config.yml with values from OpenBao at clusters/equestria/apps/forgejo/runner. Identity comes from Forgejo's offline registration (forgejo-cli actions register --secret <40 hex>), the only method that avoids pasting a UI value on every rebuild: uuid is the hex encoding of the secret's first 16 characters, so re-running with the same prefix rotates in place instead of creating a second runner.

nodes.label: forgejo-runner HelmRelease (app-template StatefulSet)
nodes.rationale: Single-replica StatefulSet with terminationGracePeriodSeconds 1860 to match runner.shutdown_timeout of 30m. All volumes are emptyDir: runner state, the docker layer store and the generated TLS certs are all rebuildable, and dropping the PVC removed an RWO detach wait on every reschedule (a 10Gi Longhorn volume at 3 replicas protected nothing). docker-storage sizeLimit 60Gi is the real bound on disk appetite since workflow code is arbitrary and capacity allows four concurrent jobs on nodes that also carry Plex/*arr/Immich, where the kubelet evicts by QoS class rather than by culprit.

nodes.label: forgejo-runner Flux Kustomization
nodes.rationale: Depends on forgejo (wait: true) because the daemon exits if it cannot reach the instance at startup. No components/volsync: everything on the runner's volume is rebuildable or already in the forge. Not Tier 1 — no critical-tier class, no control-plane toleration, bulk longhorn — so during Low Power it goes Pending rather than being scaled to 0 (it inherits coder's namespace-wide kube-downscaler exclusion, but the effect is cosmetic since it has nowhere to schedule). Either way CI waits out the window.

nodes.label: forgejo-runner kustomization.yaml (config.yml ConfigMap generator)
nodes.rationale: Generates ${APP}-config from resources/config.yml with disableNameSuffixHash so the ExternalSecret's templateFrom can reference it by a stable name.

nodes.label: forgejo-runner.rules PrometheusRule
nodes.rationale: Everything is inferred from kube-state-metrics because forgejo-runner exports no metrics and Forgejo's collector has no runner series. ForgejoRunnerDown fires on zero ready StatefulSet replicas; ForgejoRunnerFlapping on >3 container restarts/hour, which also catches a crash-looping dind sidecar that leaves the pod Ready while every job fails. No disk-bound alert: ephemeral_storage_pod_usage_bytes, container_fs_usage_bytes and kube_pod_status_reason were all checked against this cluster's Prometheus and are absent or empty, so both drafted rules would have been dead rules.

nodes.label: ClusterSecretStore remoteNamespace pins secrets to one namespace
nodes.norm_label: clustersecretstore remotenamespace pins secrets to one namespace
nodes.rationale: A ClusterSecretStore that reads in-cluster Secrets is scoped by remoteNamespace, so any app deployed outside that namespace silently fails with 'could not get secret data from provider'. The durable answer is a namespace-independent backend (OpenBao) keyed by cluster/app path, not per-namespace copies of the Secret.

nodes.label: PodMonitor over ServiceMonitor because component commonLabels break Service selectors
nodes.norm_label: podmonitor over servicemonitor because component commonlabels break service selectors
nodes.rationale: The postgres/tailscale components apply commonLabels that kustomize also injects into Service selectors, which then no longer match Helm-created pods. Scraping pods directly with a PodMonitor sidesteps the hand-written Service entirely.

nodes.label: backup-exclude needs a /** suffix (rclone bare-dir exclude is a no-op)
nodes.norm_label: backup-exclude needs a /** suffix (rclone bare-dir exclude is a no-op)
nodes.rationale: rclone's --exclude matches FILES on a bare path, so 'actions_artifacts/' would exclude nothing and quietly back the whole prefix up; the load-bearing form is 'actions_artifacts/**'. Cross-referenced to the exclude note in components/BackupPlanOrchestrator.ts.

nodes.label: At Garage factor 1 the block layer must be replicated (longhorn-critical)
nodes.norm_label: at garage factor 1 the block layer must be replicated (longhorn-critical)
nodes.rationale: garage-system can sit on a 1-replica storage class because Garage itself keeps 3 copies across 3 nodes, so the block layer is allowed to be disposable. At factor 1 Garage keeps exactly one copy, so a single-replica block layer means no redundancy at any layer and one Longhorn replica loss is total object loss. longhorn-critical (3 replicas pinned to critical-tagged control planes) is also what makes this Tier 1, matching Forgejo — the consequence is object-storage IO landing on control-plane SATA, accepted for 20Gi of one forge's LFS. PVC retention Retain on both scaled and deleted is the only thing between a scale-to-0 and total loss on a Delete-reclaim class.

nodes.label: dind native sidecar with TLS client verification
nodes.norm_label: dind native sidecar with tls client verification
nodes.rationale: A native sidecar (restartPolicy: Always on an initContainer) so the kubelet starts Docker BEFORE the runner, which logs a hard error if the daemon is unreachable at startup. DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR=/certs is the only way to keep an unauthenticated daemon off the pod network: dockerd-entrypoint.sh unconditionally prepends its OWN --host (tcp://0.0.0.0:2376 with TLS, 2375 without), so an attempt to pass --host=tcp://127.0.0.1:2375 became a second --host on the same port, dockerd died on 'port is already allocated', and each crash-loop briefly exposed an unauthenticated daemon on a routable pod IP. With a certdir the entrypoint mints a CA plus server and client certs and starts with --tlsverify, so the 0.0.0.0 listener is useless without the client key only the runner holds. privileged+root is unavoidable for cgroup/mount/iptables management, which is why it runs in its own pod rather than alongside the forge.

nodes.label: Silent-idle runner is unobservable without a canary workflow
nodes.norm_label: silent-idle runner is unobservable without a canary workflow
nodes.rationale: A runner whose poller has stopped but whose process is alive keeps its pod Ready, so no kube-state-metrics rule can fire while Forgejo queues workflows indefinitely. The TCP liveness probe on the cache port narrows this to hung/deadlocked processes (which then surface as flapping) but cannot distinguish healthy-and-idle from healthy-with-no-work. Closing it properly needs a scheduled canary workflow whose absence alerts; left deliberately undone rather than papered over with a rule that cannot fire.

nodes.label: tool_loop_guardrails hard stops
nodes.rationale: Upstream ships hard stops OFF, reasonable for interactive use where a person can see repeated tool-call warnings, and explicitly wrong for unattended gateway deployments. This is an unattended gateway deployment, so hard_stop_enabled is true with exact_failure 5, same_tool_failure 8, idempotent_no_progress 5.

nodes.label: net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 sysctl
nodes.rationale: The Dockge LXCs have no IPv6 egress (ipv6_method: none), but huggingface.co resolves to AAAA records and llama.cpp's HTTP client does not fall back to IPv4 the way curl does — every -hf model download fails instantly with 'HTTPLIB failed: Could not establish connection'. Disabling IPv6 inside the container forces the v4 path. Verified on celestia 2026-08-03.

nodes.label: Disabled OpenEBS Engines (zfs, lvm, mayastor, loki, alloy, minio)
nodes.norm_label: disabled openebs engines (zfs, lvm, mayastor, loki, alloy, minio)

nodes.label: Pulumi Backend Prefix List (applications, authentik, gulf-of-mexico, home, ocracoke, unifi-network, vault)
nodes.norm_label: pulumi backend prefix list (applications, authentik, gulf-of-mexico, home, ocracoke, unifi-network, vault)

nodes.label: Privileged Pod Security Enforcement for openebs-system
nodes.norm_label: privileged pod security enforcement for openebs-system

nodes.label: NODE_OPTIONS Heap Cap Below Container Limit
nodes.norm_label: node_options heap cap below container limit

nodes.label: AuthentikApplicationResources (applications and providers)
nodes.rationale: Applications are created from Kubernetes CRDs (ApplicationDefinition, ClusterDefinition) rather than being enumerated in code, so adding an app to a cluster is a cluster-side change; the same component mints OAuth2 client IDs/secrets and wires the per-cluster outposts.

nodes.label: Extension methods for flows and bindings
nodes.norm_label: extension methods for flows and bindings

nodes.label: Authentik flows (login, enrollment, MFA, user settings)
nodes.norm_label: authentik flows (login, enrollment, mfa, user settings)
nodes.rationale: Flows are the ordered container the stages bind into; source authentication flows exist specifically to integrate the external Tailscale and Plex sources.

nodes.label: Kubernetes CRD integration and per-cluster outposts
nodes.norm_label: kubernetes crd integration and per-cluster outposts
nodes.rationale: Reads ApplicationDefinition/ClusterDefinition CRDs plus ConfigMaps and Secrets, and manages kubeconfigs for remote clusters so one Authentik install can serve outposts on several clusters.

nodes.label: 1Password secret integration for the Authentik stack
nodes.norm_label: 1password secret integration for the authentik stack
nodes.rationale: The C# original used a native OnePassword Pulumi provider; the TypeScript port deliberately reuses the repo's existing OPClient from components/op.ts instead of adding a second 1Password access path.

nodes.label: Authorization policies (expression, group-based, default group assignment)
nodes.norm_label: authorization policies (expression, group-based, default group assignment)

nodes.label: Authentik stages (authentication, authenticator, consent, invalidation, prompt)
nodes.norm_label: authentik stages (authentication, authenticator, consent, invalidation, prompt)

nodes.label: authentik stack (Pulumi project: applications)
nodes.rationale: Declared project name is `applications`, not `authentik`. Per stacks/vault/Pulumi.yaml the project name is embedded in every resource URN, so the historical name is kept deliberately to avoid Pulumi treating the stack as a brand-new project and recreating/orphaning every resource.

nodes.label: authentik stack secrets encryptionsalt
nodes.rationale: Stack-settings file carries only an encryptionsalt: config secrets are passphrase-encrypted (PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE) rather than stored as plaintext, matching the repo safety rule that no plaintext credentials are committed.

nodes.label: Authentik Pulumi Stack (TypeScript)
nodes.rationale: Manages a full Authentik SSO installation — groups, OAuth2 scope mappings, flows, providers, external sources, Kubernetes outposts and 1Password secret storage — as code so the identity provider is reproducible.

nodes.label: backups Pulumi project
nodes.rationale: Configures backups for homelab services; one of the stacks whose project name matches its directory (unlike authentik/unifi-network/vault).

nodes.label: gulf-of-mexico Pulumi project (luna Proxmox host)
nodes.rationale: Remote Proxmox host at a friend's house (luna machine) gets its own stack so off-site hardware can be previewed and deployed independently of the on-premises estate.

nodes.label: home Pulumi project
nodes.rationale: Base homelab services stack; the canonical stack usage example for the repo.

nodes.label: home-operations stack secrets encryptionsalt
nodes.rationale: Stack file is named Pulumi.home-operations.yaml while the project is `home`, so the selected stack name (home-operations) differs from the directory and project name.

nodes.label: ocracoke Pulumi project (skystar Proxmox host)
nodes.rationale: Second remote Proxmox host at a friend's house (skystar machine), split into its own stack for the same off-site isolation reason as gulf-of-mexico.

nodes.label: system Pulumi project
nodes.rationale: Holds estate configuration that other stacks read — cluster definitions are published to OpenBao so consumer stacks depend on published secrets rather than on cross-stack references.

nodes.label: unifi-network stack (Pulumi project: applications)
nodes.rationale: Carries the project name `applications` and an authentik-copied description for the same historical URN-stability reason documented in stacks/vault/Pulumi.yaml; the metadata does not describe what the stack actually manages (UniFi network configuration).

nodes.label: vault stack (Pulumi project: applications)
nodes.rationale: Migrated from the david-driscoll/vault repo on 2026-08-22 with its state left at s3://home-operations/vault. The project name is part of every resource URN (urn:pulumi:vault::applications::...), so renaming it to `vault` would make Pulumi see a new project and recreate every TailnetKey, GitHub App token, Secret patch and webhook while orphaning the originals.

nodes.label: C#-to-TypeScript conversion of the Authentik project
nodes.norm_label: c#-to-typescript conversion of the authentik project
nodes.rationale: Port of stargate-command-cluster/pulumi/authentik from C#. Trade-offs called out: Mapperly object mapping must be hand-written in TypeScript, the tight Kubernetes integration must be redone with @pulumi/kubernetes or a K8s client, LINQ queries become array operations, and the native OnePassword provider is replaced by the repo's own OPClient. The document is internally inconsistent — it declares the conversion complete while also listing flows, stages, policies and application resources as still to be converted.

nodes.label: Node.js runtime with tsx/esm loader (no compile step)
nodes.norm_label: node.js runtime with tsx/esm loader (no compile step)
nodes.rationale: Every stack declares runtime nodejs with typescript:false and nodeargs `--import tsx/esm`. Pulumi therefore executes TypeScript directly through the tsx ESM loader instead of relying on Pulumi's built-in ts-node path, so no separate build/compile step exists and path aliases resolve at runtime.

nodes.label: Pulumi URN project-name stability constraint
nodes.rationale: A Pulumi project name is embedded in every resource URN, so changing it is equivalent to declaring a new project: all resources are re-created and the previous ones are orphaned in the estate. This is why three unrelated stack directories (authentik, unifi-network, vault) all declare the project name `applications`.

nodes.label: IGDB credentials from Twitch developer token
nodes.norm_label: igdb credentials from twitch developer token

nodes.label: API-key Query Param Auth Bypass Route
nodes.norm_label: api-key query param auth bypass route

nodes.label: immich machine-learning container
nodes.rationale: Requests amd.com/gpu: 1 on both requests and limits and mounts the shared claim at /cache and /.cache so model downloads persist across restarts.

nodes.label: fix-run-perms init container
nodes.rationale: Runs busybox as root to chown /run to 1001:1001 because the emptyDir mounted there is created root-owned and the non-root main container cannot write to it.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: dynacat
nodes.rationale: Points at ./dashboard in a different repo than the components it references; deliberately carries no substituteFrom and pins both VolSync capacity variables.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: FreshRSS
nodes.rationale: Declares the Authentik confidential OAuth2 client (redirect URIs on both the root and tailscale domains), the friends/family access policy, and a Gatus check that treats HTTP 401 as healthy because the route is behind the local-user middleware.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: freshrss-env
nodes.rationale: Fans three stores into one env Secret: openbao (crypto key), the database store (postgres_* rewrite) and the cluster store (oidc_* rewrite), so OIDC, DB and crypto credentials all arrive through a single envFrom.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: freshrss
nodes.rationale: app-template release running the container as root (runAsNonRoot false, uid/gid 0) because the FreshRSS image manages its own permissions; extensions are an emptyDir so only /var/www/FreshRSS/data is persisted.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: freshrss
nodes.rationale: Depends on volsync, postgres and external-secrets, and pulls in the postgres, tailscale, volsync and fast-node-eviction components.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Immich
nodes.rationale: Registers redirect URIs for both the immich.* and photos.* hostnames on root and tailscale domains plus the app.immich:// mobile callback in strict matching mode, and adds an immich_role property mapping with claims in the ID token.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: immich-config
nodes.rationale: Renders config.json from the immich-config ConfigMap through templateFrom, injecting the oidc_* values so the Immich config file is a Secret rather than a plain ConfigMap.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: immich-env
nodes.rationale: Carries the postgres_* rewrite plus the fixed service coordinates: valkey.database.svc.cluster.local for Redis and the in-namespace machine-learning URL on port 3003.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: immich
nodes.rationale: Runs the server and machine-learning containers in one controller as uid 568 with a wide supplementalGroups list for NFS access; the HTTPRoute serves both immich.* and photos.* and matches an X-Api-Key header rule ahead of the catch-all so API clients still traverse the local-user middleware.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: immich
nodes.rationale: Adds the postgres/superuser component and sets TAILSCALE_HOST to photos plus ReadWriteMany VolSync access modes; depends on volsync, postgres, valkey and external-secrets.

nodes.label: Kustomize overlay: immich
nodes.rationale: Generates the immich-config ConfigMap from resources/config.json with disableNameSuffixHash so the ExternalSecret template can reference it by a stable name.

nodes.label: PersistentVolume: spike-data-immich
nodes.rationale: Static 2Ti nfs-csi volume against ${SPIKE_IP}:/mnt/stash/data/immich with nfsvers=4.2, nconnect=8 and Retain reclaim, so the photo library survives PVC deletion.

nodes.label: PersistentVolumeClaim: spike-data-immich
nodes.rationale: Binds the static PV by volumeName; carries the kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/force label so Flux can replace it despite immutable fields.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Karakeep
nodes.rationale: Family-only access policy; the Authentik client uses subMode user_email with claims in the ID token to match NextAuth's custom provider callback.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: karakeep-env
nodes.rationale: Disables password auth and signups and forces OAUTH_AUTO_REDIRECT so Authentik is the only login path; pulls karakeep's own NEXTAUTH_SECRET from openbao and the OIDC fields from the cluster store populated by the applications Pulumi stack.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: karakeep
nodes.rationale: Runs as uid 1001 with an emptyDir at /run; the persistence block reserves a meilisearch subPath mount alongside karakeep's own /data, anticipating a colocated search container.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: karakeep
nodes.rationale: Its only dependsOn is the in-namespace meilisearch Kustomization, reflecting that search is a hard startup dependency rather than a platform one.

nodes.label: equestria/home app roster
nodes.rationale: Single entry point listing each app's ks.yaml; enabling or disabling an app in the home namespace is a one-line change here.

nodes.label: Omitting substituteFrom on purpose
nodes.rationale: components/common patches a substituteFrom onto every Kustomization in the estate, and a strategic-merge patch REPLACES a plain list rather than merging into it, so anything declared locally silently loses cluster-secrets/shared-secrets. Nothing under ./dashboard needs it because the ConfigMaps holding ${GITHUB_TOKEN} are annotated substitute: disabled and glance expands the value at runtime.

nodes.label: VOLSYNC_CACHE_CAPACITY pinned to 2Gi
nodes.rationale: Both movers read one variable but the defaults are asymmetric (2Gi in the ReplicationSource, 8Gi in the ReplicationDestination). The source has run on 2Gi for 83 days against a tiny restic repository, so pinning changes nothing today and prevents a future volsync-restore from provisioning an 8Gi longhorn-cache volume to restore a 5Gi source. Same pin as crowdsec-ui (#2987) and tsiam (sgc#1739).

nodes.label: volsync-restore must be removed after a restore
nodes.norm_label: volsync-restore must be removed after a restore
nodes.rationale: Leaving ../kubernetes/components/volsync-restore in the components list permanently caused the 2026-07 Longhorn incident (vault#120): the restore-once trigger had already fired, the nightly volsync-system/restore-cleanup CronJob reaped the ReplicationDestination at 03:30, and Flux recreated it on the next reconcile, re-running a full restic restore and re-provisioning a 5Gi longhorn-snapshot plus 8Gi longhorn-cache PVC pair every day.

nodes.label: Low Power keep-list via downscaler/exclude
nodes.rationale: A per-workload downscaler/exclude annotation beats the namespace-wide downscaler/force-downtime toggle (scaler.py define_scope), so annotated controllers survive the equestria low-power window. Documented in docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md.

nodes.label: FreshRSS survives credential rotation because PHP connects per request
nodes.norm_label: freshrss survives credential rotation because php connects per request
nodes.rationale: Preflighted in tranche 2: reloader.stakater.com/auto sits on the Deployment (not the pod template) and the pod reads its credential from the freshrss-env Secret, so the 30-day rotation reaches it. FreshRSS is PHP and connects per request, holding no pooled connection to invalidate at cutover; proof came from pg_stat_database.xact_commit advancing, not from pg_stat_activity.

nodes.label: Removing the phantom 1Password default store
nodes.rationale: Every dataFrom carries an explicit sourceRef, so the default secretStoreRef was never consulted; it named onepassword-connect purely by inheritance from the copied template. Repointing it at the store actually in use removes a phantom 1Password dependency Phase 11 would otherwise have to chase down.

nodes.label: immich requires a superuser role that rotation preserves
nodes.norm_label: immich requires a superuser role that rotation preserves
nodes.rationale: immich installs extensions (vectors/vchord) into its own database at startup, so it needs superuser. A DatabaseRole ADOPTS an existing role and forces every attribute to match the manifest, so the attribute must be restated or the live role is silently demoted. It has to be a component rather than a substitution because booleans cannot pass through postBuild.substitute. immich was migrated last (tranche 9) to prove that OpenBao rotation issues only ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD, leaving rolsuper true and all 8 extensions intact.

nodes.label: MEILI_MASTER_KEY must be Meilisearch's own master key
nodes.norm_label: meili_master_key must be meilisearch's own master key
nodes.rationale: The value is the master key of the Meilisearch instance karakeep points at, not karakeep's own secret. Meilisearch enforces auth now, so any other value is a 403 on every search. NEXTAUTH_SECRET is karakeep's own and is correctly unrelated.

nodes.label: karakeep, outline and collabora are commented out of the roster
nodes.norm_label: karakeep, outline and collabora are commented out of the roster
nodes.rationale: karakeep/ks.yaml, outline/ks.yaml and collabora/ks.yaml are present on disk but commented out of resources, so their manifests are inert: Flux never creates the Kustomizations and prune leaves nothing behind. The directories are kept for a future re-enable.

nodes.label: Orphan deletionPolicy for the GarageCluster identity
nodes.norm_label: orphan deletionpolicy for the garagecluster identity
nodes.rationale: The GarageCluster CR is the identity of the object store: its StatefulSets, their PVCs and the Garage layout all hang off it, so ownership changes must orphan rather than cascade-delete.

nodes.label: wait:false so Low Power mode cannot stall dependents
nodes.norm_label: wait:false so low power mode cannot stall dependents
nodes.rationale: wait: true would block the Kustomization on GarageCluster reaching Ready, and Ready requires three schedulable bulk workers. In Low Power mode (D6) there are none, so the Kustomization would sit failing for the whole window and drag every dependent with it. Health is judged by the Gatus endpoint in definition.yaml instead.

nodes.label: Operator tolerates control-plane so it survives Low Power mode
nodes.norm_label: operator tolerates control-plane so it survives low power mode
nodes.rationale: The operator is a controller, not a data plane — it belongs with the control plane so it survives Low Power mode (D6) and can resume reconciling the moment the storage tier returns. The Garage nodes themselves stay on the bulk workers.

nodes.label: crds.keep=true guards against uninstall data loss
nodes.norm_label: crds.keep=true guards against uninstall data loss
nodes.rationale: Deleting a CRD deletes every custom resource of that kind, and for GarageCluster that reaches all the way down to the PVCs. keep is the chart default, restated because it is the difference between an uninstall and a data loss.

nodes.label: grafana_dashboard label must be "true", not "1"
nodes.rationale: kube-prometheus-stack's sidecar is configured with labelValue: "true" in grafana/helmrelease.yaml, so a ConfigMap labelled "1" carries the right key with the wrong value and is silently skipped — no error anywhere, the dashboard just never appears.

nodes.label: Self-signed webhook issuer instead of estate ClusterIssuers
nodes.norm_label: self-signed webhook issuer instead of estate clusterissuers
nodes.rationale: An empty issuerName makes the chart render its own self-signed Issuer in the namespace. The estate ClusterIssuers mint publicly trusted certs through ACME/DNS-01, and burning rate limit on a webhook cert only the apiserver validates (against the chart-injected CA bundle) would be waste.

nodes.label: cert-manager-controller is a hard prerequisite for admission
nodes.norm_label: cert-manager-controller is a hard prerequisite for admission
nodes.rationale: The chart's admission and conversion webhooks are on by default and their certificates come from cert-manager. Without the controller the HelmRelease installs a Certificate that never issues, the webhook Service has no serving cert, and every GarageCluster/Bucket/Key apply fails at admission — which looks like a broken CRD rather than a missing issuer.

nodes.label: Chart publishes SLSA provenance, not a cosign signature
nodes.norm_label: chart publishes slsa provenance, not a cosign signature
nodes.rationale: verify: { provider: cosign } was rejected by Flux with 'can't verify identities without providing at least one identity'. That message reads like a missing matchOIDCIdentity but is not: at this digest there is no sha256-<digest>.sig tag and the referrers index holds one artifact, a SLSA build provenance attestation (dev.sigstore.bundle, dsse-envelope). Flux's cosign provider verifies signatures and has no path to consume a SLSA attestation, so no identity regex could make it pass. Verify out-of-band with `gh attestation verify`; the digest pin is what actually protects the pull.

nodes.label: Reloader auto-restart on Connect credential rotation
nodes.norm_label: reloader auto-restart on connect credential rotation
nodes.rationale: reloader.stakater.com/auto is set on both the deployment and the service so the Connect pods restart when the sops-managed 1password-credentials.json Secret changes; the operator sub-chart is disabled (operator.create: false) because only the Connect API is wanted here.

nodes.label: github-actions namespace runs pod-security enforce=privileged
nodes.rationale: Self-hosted Actions runners need to build and run containers, so the namespace label pins pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce to privileged rather than the estate default baseline/restricted.

nodes.label: ARC controller and scale-set charts pinned in lockstep at 0.14.2
nodes.norm_label: arc controller and scale-set charts pinned in lockstep at 0.14.2
nodes.rationale: Both OCIRepositories track the same tag because the gha-runner-scale-set listener protocol is only compatible with a matching controller version; splitting the versions breaks runner registration.

nodes.label: mosquitto-secret SOPS Secret (users, pwd file, per-replica confs)
nodes.norm_label: mosquitto-secret sops secret (users, pwd file, per-replica confs)

nodes.label: deletionPolicy Orphan for the live home-automation namespace
nodes.norm_label: deletionpolicy orphan for the live home-automation namespace

nodes.label: longhorn-critical VolSync storage tier for Matter
nodes.norm_label: longhorn-critical volsync storage tier for matter

nodes.label: Tier-1 control-plane tolerations and critical-tier priority for Mosquitto
nodes.norm_label: tier-1 control-plane tolerations and critical-tier priority for mosquitto

nodes.label: kubeproxy ProxyGroup (kube-apiserver auth mode)
nodes.rationale: Tier 1: this ProxyGroup is how the tailnet reaches the Kubernetes API, so it must remain placeable on a control plane during a low-power window; it therefore uses the control-plane-tolerant ProxyClass rather than default.

nodes.label: default ProxyClass
nodes.rationale: Baseline ProxyClass: enables metrics plus a ServiceMonitor and stamps a reloader auto annotation on the generated StatefulSet. acceptRoutes is deliberately left commented out.

nodes.label: tailnet-cluster-ops ClusterRole
nodes.rationale: Mirrors definition-crds permissions plus notification.toolkit.fluxcd.io read access, for devices impersonated as tailnet-cluster-ops through kubeproxy auth mode. garage.rajsingh.info is granted at cluster scope because stacks/applications' garageBucketBackups lists GarageBuckets cluster-wide; kubernetes-backups.ts deliberately rethrows anything that is not a 404, so a 403 aborts the whole applications stack instead of silently reporting no buckets and leaving opted-in buckets unprotected. resources: [*] is used rather than a single resource name because read-only on one operator's own API group is not a boundary worth re-editing.

nodes.label: blackbox-probe-alerts PrometheusRule
nodes.rationale: Single shared alert set over probe_success/probe_duration_seconds for every Probe in this directory; remote=true targets get much longer for: windows (2h/30m vs 10m/2m) because off-site links flap.

nodes.label: tailnet-inbound ProxyGroup
nodes.rationale: Shared ingress ProxyGroup that every per-host ExternalName Service targets via the tailscale.com/proxy-group annotation; defined in inbound.yaml and aggregated by this kustomization.

nodes.label: control-plane-tolerant ProxyClass
nodes.rationale: A ProxyGroup exposes no pod-spec fields of its own, so spec.proxyClass is the only route to the generated StatefulSet pod template. Kept separate from default rather than folded into it because default also carries a reloader annotation and its members (tailnet-inbound/-outbound) are not Tier 1. The control-plane toleration only widens where a pod MAY schedule once allowSchedulingOnControlPlanes goes false; it pins nothing. Metrics intentionally match default because a Tier-1 proxy surviving a low-power window is the last one that should go unscraped.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: OpenBooks
nodes.rationale: driscoll.dev/v1 ApplicationDefinition is the estate's single declaration point for an app's identity: it drives the Authentik forward_single proxy provider, the media-managers access policy, and the Gatus HTTP check, so those three concerns never drift apart per-app.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: openbooks
nodes.rationale: IRC book-fetch daemon (evanbuss/openbooks) run with --persist and --no-browser-downloads so downloads land on the shared truenas-media claim under downloads/openbooks instead of being streamed to a browser.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: openbooks
nodes.rationale: Pulls in the shared tailscale and volsync components and substitutes APP/NAMESPACE, so the HelmRelease can template ${APP}.${ROOT_DOMAIN} without repeating the app name.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: bookbounty-audio
nodes.rationale: Sidecar acquisition helper for the audio Readarr instance; sync_schedule is 12 (offset from the ebook instance's 0) so the two BookBounty instances never hit libgen or Readarr at the same hour.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Readarr Audio
nodes.rationale: Restricted to the media-managers group, unlike the ebook instance which is opened to family and friends — the audio instance is an operator tool, not a patron-facing library.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: readarr-audio
nodes.rationale: Second Readarr instance (INSTANCENAME 'Readarr (Audio)') sharing the same image, port 8787, API key secret and truenas-media mounts as the ebook instance; only the config PVC (readarr-audio-config) is distinct, which is what keeps the two libraries separate.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: readarr-audio
nodes.rationale: dependsOn the readarr Kustomization because the shared readarr-apikey Secret is only rendered by the readarr-ebook directory; ordering the audio instance behind it avoids a start with a missing secretKeyRef.

nodes.label: Secret: readarr-apikey (SOPS/age)
nodes.rationale: One age-encrypted API key shared by BOTH Readarr instances and BOTH BookBounty helpers, so a rotation is a single-file change; it is the only SOPS secret in the books tree (everything else moved to ExternalSecrets).

nodes.label: HelmRelease: bookbounty
nodes.rationale: Ebook-side acquisition helper; both BookBounty instances write into the SAME truenas-media subPath downloads/bookbounty, so the on-disk staging area is shared even though the config PVCs are not.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Readarr Ebook
nodes.rationale: access_policy grants family and friends (not media-managers), marking the ebook instance as the patron-facing one of the pair.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: readarr
nodes.rationale: Primary Readarr; READARR__AUTH__METHOD External with REQUIRED DisabledForLocalAddresses defers authentication to the Authentik forward-auth middleware on the HTTPRoute while leaving in-cluster API calls (BookBounty) unauthenticated apart from the API key.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: readarr
nodes.rationale: Named 'readarr' (not 'readarr-ebook') even though its path is books/readarr-ebook — the audio instance's dependsOn refers to this name, so the directory/name mismatch is load-bearing.

nodes.label: Secret: technitium-pkcs12-password
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a plaintext literal ('technitium') rather than a real secret: it only protects the keystore file inside the cluster, and the same value must be typed into the Technitium API as the per-node certificate password after the node joins.

nodes.label: Certificate: technitium-tls
nodes.rationale: letsencrypt-production cert for ${CLUSTER_CNAME}.dns.${ROOT_DOMAIN} with a PKCS12 keystore, because Technitium's per-node cluster TLS wants a pkcs12 file rather than a PEM pair.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Technitium DNS
nodes.rationale: Unlike the books apps this one declares an authentik oauth2 (confidential) client rather than a proxy provider, because Technitium performs its own OIDC SSO against ${CLUSTER_KEY}.dns.${ROOT_DOMAIN}:53443/sso/callback. Two Gatus checks cover both the 53443 cluster port and the plain admin route.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: technitium-env
nodes.rationale: Pulls the admin password from the shared apps/technitium/admin path but the OIDC triple from the per-cluster clusters/equestria/apps/technitium/oidc path; deletionPolicy Retain keeps DNS alive if OpenBao is sealed.

nodes.label: tailscale sidecar (dns-${CLUSTER_CNAME})
nodes.rationale: Deliberately a sidecar rather than the Tailscale operator's L3 ingress: the operator could only ever serve INBOUND traffic, but Technitium's outbound cluster traffic (zone refresh, config sync, heartbeats) must source from the same registered tailnet IP. TS_KUBE_SECRET is blanked so state lives on the volsync PVC (subPath .tailscale-state) instead of a kube Secret, and TS_ACCEPT_DNS is false so the cluster resolver stays intact.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: technitium
nodes.rationale: Runs as root with NET_BIND_SERVICE so it can hold :53, attaches the technitium-dns-net ipvlan NAD for direct LAN DNS, and keeps its DNS_SERVER_* env in lockstep with docker/_common/technitium/.env — those vars are first-start-only once /etc/dns exists, after which cluster sync owns the settings.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: technitium
nodes.rationale: Targets the network namespace (not equestria) and uses wait:false with an explicit HelmRelease healthCheck, because the ipvlan-attached pod's readiness is judged by the HR rather than by generic resource readiness.

nodes.label: busybox chown/chmod restore initContainer
nodes.rationale: Repeated verbatim in openbooks, readarr, readarr-audio and both bookbounty releases: a root initContainer named 'restore' chowns the config path to 568:568 before the non-root app starts. It exists because volsync restores land with the mover's ownership, so without it a restored PVC would be unwritable by uid 568.

nodes.label: local-user Traefik middleware filter
nodes.rationale: Every books HTTPRoute attaches the same ExtensionRef filter (traefik.io Middleware 'local-user') in the network namespace. This is the estate's uniform 'authenticate at the edge, trust in-cluster' boundary; the app containers themselves run with External auth and no built-in login.

nodes.label: Static private key pinned by DANE TLSA
nodes.norm_label: static private key pinned by dane tlsa
nodes.rationale: privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never. The Technitium cluster's DANE TLSA records pin the SPKI hash, so a rotated key silently breaks node-to-node heartbeats — the failure is invisible at renewal time and only shows up as cluster desync.

nodes.label: Control-plane pinning via technitium-dns nodeLabel
nodes.rationale: nodeSelector technitium-dns=true moved off hard-hat 2026-08-19 onto milky-way/othalla/pegasus so the LAN resolver survives a low-power window with every worker off. The control-plane NoSchedule toleration is mandatory — a nodeSelector matching only tainted nodes without it yields an unschedulable pod.

nodes.label: exec-based health probes (127.0.0.1:5380)
nodes.rationale: tcpSocket probes are dialed by the kubelet from the node's LAN IP, but the pod answers out the ipvlan net1 interface — asymmetric routing means they always time out, the pod never goes Ready, and every Service loses its endpoints. Bash /dev/tcp exec probes run inside the pod and dodge the routing entirely.

nodes.label: Tier-1 longhorn-critical storage selection
nodes.rationale: VOLSYNC_STORAGECLASS overridden to longhorn-critical (3 replicas, one per control plane) with longhorn-critical-snapshot/-cache scratch classes, so estate DNS keeps working — and can still be backed up and restored — with the workers powered down. Migrated from the component's longhorn default 2026-08-19 via the piece-13 choreography (final sync, RD restore, PVC recreate).

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: meilisearch-env
nodes.rationale: Pulls the master key from OpenBao path clusters/equestria/apps/meilisearch/secret-key (was the 1Password item 'MeiliSearch Secret Key') and rewrites every field to a meili_ prefix so the template can address it as .meili_password.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: meilisearch
nodes.rationale: Broken out of karakeep into a standalone release so the search engine can be versioned and upgraded independently. Uses the upstream meilisearch chart (0.38.0) rather than app-template because the chart owns the StatefulSet, persistence and serviceMonitor wiring.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: n8n-env
nodes.rationale: Composes two stores into one env Secret: app credentials (encryption key, license key) from the OpenBao ClusterSecretStore at clusters/equestria/apps/n8n/credentials, and rotating Postgres connection fields from the `database` ClusterSecretStore item ${APP}-postgres. Carries cnpg.io/reload and reloader annotations so a rotation restarts the pod.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: n8n
nodes.rationale: app-template deployment of n8n on port 8080 behind the internal Gateway with the authenticated-user Traefik middleware. Built-in user management is disabled (N8N_USER_MANAGEMENT_DISABLED) and identity is taken from Authentik's X-Authentik-Email forward-auth header via an external hooks file, so the proxy is the only authentication boundary. A root init container chowns /config to 1000:1000 because the app runs read-only-rootfs as uid 1000.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: n8n
nodes.rationale: Opts into the rotating-credential components/postgres component. Safe here because n8n already has a ~600s startup probe (the same protection tandoor needed in #1142), so the restart a rotation forces cannot be probe-killed mid-boot; the password is read from n8n-env via envFrom.

nodes.label: ConfigMap generator: n8n-hooks
nodes.rationale: Generated from resources/hooks.js with disableNameSuffixHash and kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/substitute: disabled, so Flux post-build substitution never rewrites JavaScript that legitimately contains ${...} and the mount path stays stable.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: obsidian-sync (CouchDB)
nodes.rationale: Plain couchdb image under app-template running as uid/gid 5984 with a matching fsGroup so the Longhorn volume at /opt/couchdb/data is writable. A cors.ini ConfigMap is mounted into local.d because Obsidian LiveSync clients are browser/Electron origins; the in-container CORS config is permissive and the real origin allow-list is enforced at the Traefik edge.

nodes.label: Flux Kustomization: obsidian-sync
nodes.rationale: VOLSYNC_PUID/PGID are pinned to 5984 to match the CouchDB user, so restic restores land with ownership the container can use.

nodes.label: Traefik Middleware: obsidian-sync-cors
nodes.rationale: Edge-enforced CORS allow-list for the Obsidian client surfaces: https://app.obsidian.md (web), app://obsidian.md (desktop), capacitor://localhost and http://localhost (mobile). Headers are enumerated explicitly rather than wildcarded so credentialed requests stay valid.

nodes.label: Job: obsidian-sync-init (CouchDB bootstrap)
nodes.rationale: post-install Helm hook that polls http://obsidian-sync:5984/_up until ready, then PUTs the three system databases (_users, _replicator, _global_changes) that CouchDB will not create for itself. Credentials come from env vars rather than the URL so they never appear in the process list; each PUT is `|| true` so a re-run on an already-initialised cluster is idempotent.

nodes.label: ApplicationDefinition: Outline
nodes.rationale: Declares a confidential Authentik OAuth2 client with redirect URIs for both the public and the tailnet hostname, and subMode user_email so Outline identifies accounts by email — real OIDC rather than the forward-auth proxy mode the other apps in this directory use.

nodes.label: ExternalSecret: outline-values
nodes.rationale: Three-store fan-in (onepassword-connect for the app secret key, `database` for Postgres, `cluster` for the Authentik OIDC client) rendered through templateFrom against the ${APP}-values ConfigMap, producing a complete values.yaml as Secret data. This is the mechanism that lets the HelmRelease keep zero inline values. Unlike the other apps in this directory it still reads from 1Password rather than OpenBao.

nodes.label: HelmRelease: outline
nodes.rationale: Community chart release whose entire values document is supplied by valuesFrom a Secret (${APP}-values) instead of inline values, so the OIDC client secret and Postgres password never appear in git.

nodes.label: Standard equestria/home app component stack
nodes.rationale: Every app in equestria/home composes the same Flux components — failover/fast-node-eviction and tailscale always, plus volsync where there is state and postgres where there is a rotating database credential — and drives them with postBuild substitutions (APP, NAMESPACE, VOLSYNC_*). The component list plus the substitute map is the whole per-app deployment contract.

nodes.label: MEILI_ENV production auth enforcement
nodes.rationale: Meilisearch was pinned to MEILI_ENV=development only because the master key rendered empty and production refuses to boot on a key under 16 bytes. Now that meilisearch-env resolves a real 42-byte key from OpenBao, flipping to production makes the server ENFORCE auth. The StatefulSet carries no reloader annotation, so the Secret gaining a value never restarted the pod; editing the chart's `environment:` map changes its config checksum annotation, which rolls the pod and picks up key and setting together. Also carries MEILI_UPGRADE_DB=true for the one-way on-startup 1.47.0 -> 1.51.0 DB migration. The chart key is `environment:` (rendered into a ConfigMap consumed via envFrom), NOT `env:` — an earlier `env:` block was silently ignored (vault#102).

nodes.label: Low-power downscaler keep-list exclusion
nodes.rationale: The workload annotation downscaler/exclude: "true" survives downscaler/force-downtime applied to the whole equestria namespace, because a per-workload exclude beats the namespace toggle in scaler.py define_scope. Documented in docs/cluster-consolidation/24-power-states.md.

nodes.label: Phase 6 pilot: first ExternalSecret moved to OpenBao
nodes.norm_label: phase 6 pilot: first externalsecret moved to openbao
nodes.rationale: Chosen deliberately as the first 1Password -> OpenBao cutover: one standalone app, one key, nothing else depends on the Secret, and a failure surfaces as CouchDB rejecting auth rather than as anything cluster-wide. The key is a path inside the `secrets` mount (the store pins path: secrets, so it is not repeated), and Phase 4 migrated the item field-for-field so the `username`/`password` field names — and therefore the template — needed no edit.

nodes.label: Dropped-app parking and the postgres re-enable trap
nodes.norm_label: dropped-app parking and the postgres re-enable trap
nodes.rationale: Outline was dropped (group E, 2026-08-25) and the whole ks.yaml is parked — the parent kustomization has it commented out too, which is why the file is commented rather than deleted. The components/postgres line specifically must NOT be uncommented as a restore step: the Database CR, the database and the login role were all removed, and the Pulumi `system` stack discovers that component and creates database/static-roles/${APP}, which fails outright until CNPG has recreated the role. See the ORDER OF OPERATIONS block in components/postgres/ks.yaml.

nodes.label: traefik-crds Kustomization
nodes.rationale: deletionPolicy: Orphan is deliberate and described in-file as the highest-value place in the whole tree for it -- deleting this Kustomization must never cascade-delete the CRDs, because every instance of every kind cluster-wide would go with them. wait: false because CRDs have no readiness to wait on. See docs/cluster-consolidation/26-bootstrap-apps-to-pulumi.md.

nodes.label: Traefik + Gateway API CRD bundle
nodes.rationale: Pulls Gateway API experimental-install.yaml plus the ten traefik.io CRDs straight from raw.githubusercontent at a pinned chart tag rather than letting the Helm chart install them, so CRD lifecycle is decoupled from the HelmRelease (which sets crds: Skip on both install and upgrade). Each URL carries a renovate annotation so version bumps are automated.

nodes.label: Traefik Dashboard ApplicationDefinition
nodes.rationale: No `authentik:` block by design -- the dashboard is deliberately not behind a proxy provider (see the values.yaml middleware comment). Leaving one here would keep minting a forward_single provider that nothing routes through. Access is expressed only as an access_policy group (admins) plus a Gatus 200 check.

nodes.label: error-pages HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: tarampampam/error-pages behind an app-template chart, 2 replicas with a hostname topology spread and maxUnavailable: 1 PDB. Tier 1: must survive a Battery window when workers are off and control planes carry the low-power taint, so it carries the control-plane toleration -- added after section 8 Stage 2 found it among the 51 untolerated Tier-0/1 workloads. Liveness probe disabled; serves on port 8080.

nodes.label: external Gateway
nodes.rationale: Hand-written sibling to the chart-rendered `internal` Gateway: same gatewayClassName (traefik) and the same le-production-tls cert, but targeted at EXTERNAL_DOMAIN/EXTERNAL_IP and carrying only web + websecure (no database or gitssh listeners exposed publicly).

nodes.label: traefik HelmRelease
nodes.rationale: crds: Skip on both install and upgrade because the traefik-crds Kustomization owns CRD lifecycle. rollback.force: false (unlike error-pages) so a failed upgrade never force-recreates the ingress datapath. Values come entirely from the traefik-values ConfigMap, not inline.

nodes.label: traefik Kustomization
nodes.rationale: dependsOn traefik-crds so the CRDs exist before any Middleware/IngressRoute is applied. deletionPolicy: Orphan mirrors kube-system/cilium/ks.yaml -- traefik is ingress critical path and must not be torn out by a Kustomization deletion. Composes the failover/fast-node-eviction component.

nodes.label: traefik-values ConfigMap generator
nodes.rationale: values.yaml is delivered as a configMapGenerator with disableNameSuffixHash: true so the HelmRelease's valuesFrom can reference a stable name `traefik-values`. A JSON6902 patch strips /spec/values/defaultPodOptions from the traefik HelmRelease, undoing an inherited default that does not apply to the upstream traefik chart.

nodes.label: authenticated-user Middleware chain
nodes.rationale: Standard gated chain: error-pages -> outpost -> internal-network. Ordering matters -- error-pages wraps first so an outpost or IP rejection renders a themed page rather than a bare 401/403.

nodes.label: local-user Middleware chain
nodes.rationale: The authenticated-user chain minus the outpost hop: error-pages -> internal-network. Exists so break-glass surfaces (notably the Traefik dashboard) can be network-gated without a dependency on authentik being up.

nodes.label: cloudflare-ips ipAllowList Middleware
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare's published v4/v6 ranges, plus the RFC1918 and tailnet ranges inlined because Traefik chains do not support OR operations (traefik/traefik#6007) -- the union has to live inside a single ipAllowList rather than being composed from two.

nodes.label: crowdsec-bouncer-plugin Middleware
nodes.rationale: Named crowdsec-bouncer-plugin, NOT crowdsec-bouncer: components/common/middleware.yaml defines a per-namespace alias of that name and `network` includes components/common like every other namespace, so both manifests targeted network/crowdsec-bouncer, the alias won, and the plugin config was overwritten by a chain pointing at itself ('recursion detected in middleware'), after which Traefik dropped every router carrying the filter. The plugin key must also match experimental.plugins in values.yaml (crowdsec-bouncer-traefik-plugin) -- it previously read crowdsec-bouncer and could never resolve to a loaded plugin.

nodes.label: default-cors Middleware
nodes.rationale: Allows credentialed cross-origin requests but only from an origin regex matching any driscoll.tech subdomain over http or https, with addVaryHeader so caches key on Origin.

nodes.label: error-pages Middleware
nodes.rationale: Catches 401-599 and rewrites to /{status}.html against the error-pages Service in the network namespace on port 8080 -- the Traefik-side half of the error-pages HelmRelease deployment.

nodes.label: fail2ban plugin Middleware
nodes.rationale: Bans on 4 failures in 10m for 12h against status codes 400,401,403-499, with the same five internal ranges allowlisted -- but as a comma-separated scalar rather than a list. Commented out of middleware/kustomization.yaml, so it is not applied; it is the older in-Traefik answer to the same abuse-blocking problem the CrowdSec bouncer now owns.

nodes.label: github-hook-ips ipAllowList Middleware
nodes.rationale: GitHub's webhook source ranges from https://api.github.com/meta, maintained by hand -- narrows webhook receivers to GitHub only, with no internal ranges added (unlike cloudflare-ips).

nodes.label: host-header Middleware
nodes.rationale: Declares X-Forwarded-Host and Host as hostsProxyHeaders so apps behind cloudflared see the public hostname rather than the internal one.

nodes.label: https-redirect Middleware
nodes.rationale: Permanent scheme redirect available as a per-route middleware; largely redundant with the web entryPoint's built-in redirections block in values.yaml, which already forces every :80 request to websecure.

nodes.label: internal-network ipAllowList Middleware
nodes.rationale: Allows CLUSTER_NETWORK, SERVICE_NETWORK, RFC1918 10/8 and 192.168/16, and the tailnet CGNAT range 100.64/10 -- the same five-range set repeated in cloudflare-ips, fail2ban's allowlist, the crowdsec trusted-IP lists, and the values.yaml forwardedHeaders trustedIPs.

nodes.label: Traefik middleware bundle
nodes.rationale: crowdsec.yaml creates the bouncer Middleware in THIS namespace only and holds the plugin config including the kill switch; it is inert on its own because the plugin ships disabled. Routes do not reference this copy directly -- Traefik resolves an ExtensionRef in the route's own namespace, so each namespace gets a thin alias chaining here from components/common/middleware.yaml. fail2ban.yaml and tailscale-redirect.yaml are commented out.

nodes.label: outpost forwardAuth Middleware
nodes.rationale: forwardAuth to authentik-outpost.${CLUSTER_CNAME}:9000 with trustForwardHeader, propagating the full X-authentik-* header set (including the JWT and JWKS metadata) plus Remote-User so downstream apps can do header-based SSO.

nodes.label: traefik-tls-settings ConfigMap
nodes.rationale: Delivers store.yaml to Traefik's file provider (--providers.file.filename=/config/store.yaml) declaring both /certs (le-production-tls) and /cluster-certs (cluster-tls) certificates, with the Let's Encrypt pair as the default store certificate.

nodes.label: Traefik dashboard IngressRoute
nodes.rationale: BREAK-GLASS: network-gated, NOT authentik-gated. Uses the `local-user` chain (error-pages -> internal-network) rather than `authenticated-user` (which adds the outpost hop), because the dashboard is one of the tools used to diagnose an authentik outage and must not depend on authentik being up. A hard prerequisite of moving authentik off-cluster -- see docs/cluster-consolidation/07-authentik-to-alpha-site.md section 3.3.

nodes.label: internal Gateway
nodes.rationale: Chart-rendered Gateway named `internal` carrying six listeners (HTTP, HTTPS-Terminate, and three raw TCP database listeners plus gitssh), all with namespacePolicy from: All. Annotated for external-dns at INTERNAL_DOMAIN and pinned to INTERNAL_IP via Cilium LB-IPAM.

nodes.label: Traefik chart values
nodes.rationale: 2-replica Deployment at system-node-critical with a DoNotSchedule hostname topology spread; ingressClass name `internal` gates all three kubernetes providers (CRD, Ingress, Gateway) so only internal-classed objects are picked up. allowCrossNamespace and allowExternalNameServices are both on so routes can target services anywhere.

nodes.label: CrowdSec bouncer kill switch and fail-open posture
nodes.norm_label: crowdsec bouncer kill switch and fail-open posture
nodes.rationale: `enabled: false` is the standing rollback for every enforcement stage, because middlewares attach per-route via ExtensionRef across 74 HTTPRoutes in 69 files -- detaching at that scale is not a rollback. It does NOT skip validation: the plugin runs ValidateParams unconditionally in New(), so an empty crowdsecLapiKeyFile breaks every referencing route regardless. Deliberately fail-open: crowdsecMode stream (a LAPI outage degrades to a stale list instead of sitting in the request path), streamStartupBlock false (default true would block traffic during init until first sync), updateMaxFailure -1 (default 0 turns a LAPI restart into a 403 storm), httpTimeoutSeconds 3, remediationStatusCode 403 so a false-positive ban is distinguishable from a 5xx. Stated trade-off: fail-open makes a wrong bouncer key indistinguishable from 'no decisions' -- `cscli bouncers list` showing a recent Last API pull is the only positive proof. forwardedHeadersTrustedIPs (which proxies to trust for XFF) and clientTrustedIPs (which resolved clients to never evaluate) do different jobs; the latter is the break-glass escape hatch that survives a sick LAPI. defaultDecisionSeconds is deliberately unset -- live-mode only.

nodes.label: crowdsecLapiKeyFile / 1Password field-name coupling
nodes.rationale: The 1Password field `apikey_bouncer` on item 'Crowdsec ApiKey' is synced into the crowdsec-secret Secret by traefik/crowdsec-secret.yaml and mounted at /etc/secrets/crowdsec by values.yaml. The 1Password operator syncs field names verbatim with no rename facility, so the file name IS the field name. This previously pointed at /etc/secrets/crowdsec/lapi, a name that exists nowhere; it was repointed rather than introducing an ExternalSecret whose only job would be renaming, which would be a second mapping to keep in sync -- how it broke in the first place. The LAPI reads the same field as BOUNCER_KEY_traefik, so both ends are the same field by construction.

nodes.label: Gateway listener / entryPoint port pairing
nodes.rationale: Traefik matches a Gateway listener to an entryPoint BY PORT, so each listener (web 80, websecure 443, postgres 5432, mariadb 3306, bolt 7687, gitssh 22) must move together with its entrypoint -- a listener with no entrypoint on the same port is silently dropped, with no error.

nodes.label: gitssh entryPoint on port 22
nodes.rationale: Fronts Forgejo's built-in Go SSH server on the standard port so clone URLs stay plain git@git.driscoll.tech:owner/repo. Nothing collides: Talos nodes run no sshd and this binds the Gateway LoadBalancer IP, not a node. Traefik can take :22 as uid 65532 with all capabilities dropped because Kubernetes sets net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0 in the pod sandbox. Tailscale.ports.git in components/constants.ts grants tcp:22 and is NOT the same grant as ports.ssh. readTimeout: 0s matters for the same reason as on postgres -- a long git clone is one idle-then-bursty stream.

nodes.label: Top-level tolerations (not deployment.tolerations)
nodes.rationale: Verified against traefik 41.3.0 by rendering the chart with both keys set: only .Values.tolerations reaches the pod spec. The nested copy under `deployment:` was silently dead, so live pods carried the admission controller's DEFAULT not-ready/unreachable tolerations at tolerationSeconds 300 instead of the intended 60. The control-plane NoSchedule entry is Tier 1: traefik must survive a Battery window when workers are off and control planes carry the low-power taint. See docs/cluster-consolidation/20-low-power-tier.md section 4.
